title.en: Volume 292 Biographies 79: Gao Qizhuo, Yang Zongren, Kong Yuxun, Fei Xian Du, Tang Zhiyu, Yang Yongbin
title.raw: 卷292 列傳七十九 高其倬 杨宗仁 孔毓珣 斐幰度 唐执玉 杨永斌

sentences.zh: 列傳七十九

translations.literal: Biographies 79
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 79

sentences.zh: 高其倬金鉷楊宗仁子文乾孔毓珣裴幰度子宗錫

translations.literal: Gao Qizhuo, Jin Hong, Yang Zongren, Zi Wenqian, Kong Yuxun, Pei Xiandu, Zi Zongxi
translations.idiomatic: Gao Qizhuo, Jin Hong, Yang Zongren, Zi Wenqian, Kong Yuxun, Pei Xiandu, and Zi Zongxi

sentences.zh: 唐執玉楊永斌

translations.literal: Tang Zhiyu, Yang Yongbin
translations.idiomatic: Tang Zhiyu and Yang Yongbin

sentences.zh: 高其倬，字章之，漢軍鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Gao Qizhuo, style name Zhangzhi, was a man of the Han military Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Qizhuo, courtesy name Zhangzhi, belonged to the Han military Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 父廕爵，官口北道。

translations.literal: His father inherited a noble rank and served as commissioner of the Koubei Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: His father held an inherited noble rank and served as Koubei Circuit commissioner.

sentences.zh: 其倬，康熙三十三年進士，改庶吉士，散館授檢討。

translations.literal: Qizhuo passed the civil examination in the thirty-third year of Kangxi, was made a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and upon leaving the academy was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: Qizhuo earned his jinshi degree in Kangxi 33, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and after completing his academy term was appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 尋兼佐領。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he also served as assistant banner commander.
translations.idiomatic: He soon took an additional post as assistant banner commander.

sentences.zh: 五遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: After five promotions he became a Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: After five promotions he rose to Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，河南南陽鎮兵挾忿圍辱知府沈淵，命偕尚書張廷樞按治，誅首事者，總兵高成等論罪有差。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year, soldiers of the Nanyang garrison in Henan, nursing a grievance, besieged and humiliated Prefect Shen Yuan; he was ordered to investigate jointly with Minister Zhang Tingshu, execute the ringleaders, and punish Regional Commander Gao Cheng and others to varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: In year 58, Nanyang garrison troops in Henan, nursing a grievance, besieged and humiliated Prefect Shen Yuan. Qizhuo was ordered to investigate with Minister Zhang Tingshu, execute the ringleaders, and mete out differing punishments to Regional Commander Gao Cheng and others.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，授廣西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year he was appointed governor of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In year 59 he was appointed governor of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 鄧橫苗叛，其倬親撫之降。

translations.literal: The Dengheng Miao rebelled; Qizhuo went in person to pacify them and secured their surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When the Dengheng Miao rose in revolt, Qizhuo went in person to pacify them and brought about their surrender.

sentences.zh: 六十一年，世宗即位，擢雲貴總督。

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year, when the Shizong Emperor acceded, Qizhuo was promoted to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 61, upon the Yongzheng Emperor's accession, he was promoted to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「士司承襲，向有陋規，已嚴行禁革。

translations.literal: In a memorial he stated: "In the succession of native chieftains there have long been corrupt practices, which have already been strictly forbidden and abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Succession among native chieftains has long been marred by corrupt practices, which I have already strictly forbidden and abolished.

sentences.zh: 諮部文冊，如無大舛錯，請免駁換。

translations.literal: When the documents sent to the ministry are consulted, if there are no serious errors, I request that they be exempted from rejection and replacement."
translations.idiomatic: When the paperwork sent to the ministry is reviewed, if there are no serious errors, I ask that it be accepted without being sent back for revision."

sentences.zh: 」得旨嘉獎。

translations.literal: An imperial rescript commended him.
translations.idiomatic: The throne responded with commendation.

sentences.zh: 青海台吉羅卜藏丹津叛侵西藏，其倬以中甸為入藏要道，檄諸將劉宗魁、劉國侯等嚴為備。

translations.literal: The Qinghai taiji Lobzang Danjin rebelled and invaded Tibet; Qizhuo, holding that Zhongdian was the vital route into Tibet, ordered the generals Liu Zongkui, Liu Guohou, and others to make strict preparations.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qinghai taiji Lobzang Danjin rebelled and invaded Tibet, Qizhuo judged Zhongdian the key route into Tibet and ordered Generals Liu Zongkui, Liu Guohou, and others to prepare defenses in earnest.

sentences.zh: 並遵上指，令提督郝玉麟將二千人自中甸進駐察木多，副將孫宏本將五百人赴中甸為聲援。

translations.literal: He also followed the emperor's instructions, ordering Provincial Commander Hao Yulin to lead two thousand men from Zhongdian to advance and garrison Chamdo, and Vice Commander Sun Hongben to lead five hundred men to Zhongdian as reinforcement.
translations.idiomatic: Following the emperor's instructions, he ordered Provincial Commander Hao Yulin to march two thousand men from Zhongdian to garrison Chamdo, and Vice Commander Sun Hongben to bring five hundred men to Zhongdian as support.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年，師定青海，中甸喇嘛、番酋等率三千五百戶納土請降。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongzheng, after the army pacified Qinghai, the lamas, tribal chiefs, and others of Zhongdian led thirty-five hundred households in surrendering their territory and submitting.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 2, after the army pacified Qinghai, Zhongdian lamas and tribal chiefs led thirty-five hundred households in surrendering their lands.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其倬能，予世職拜他喇布勒哈番。

translations.literal: The emperor praised Qizhuo's ability and granted him a hereditary office as Baitalabuleha fan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised Qizhuo's ability and granted him a hereditary rank as Baitalabuleha fan.

sentences.zh: 其倬規畫安撫中甸，疏「請設同知以下官：番酋營官外，又有神翁、列賓諸號，聽堪布、喇嘛指揮，請改授守備、千把總劄付，聽將吏統轄。

translations.literal: Qizhuo planned the pacification of Zhongdian and memorialized: "I request the appointment of officials down to the rank of subprefect; besides the tribal chiefs' camp officers there are also titles such as shenweng and liebin, who take orders from khenpos and lamas—I request that they be reappointed with commissions as garrison commanders, battalion officers, and platoon leaders, subject to the command of military officers.
translations.idiomatic: Qizhuo drew up plans to pacify Zhongdian and memorialized: "I ask that officials be appointed down to subprefect. Besides the tribal chiefs' camp officers, there are also ranks such as shenweng and liebin, who answer to khenpos and lamas. I propose reappointing them with military commissions as garrison commanders, battalion officers, and platoon leaders under regular officers."

sentences.zh: 僧寺喇嘛以三百為限，收兵械入官。

translations.literal: Monks and lamas in temples were limited to three hundred, and weapons were confiscated for the government.
translations.idiomatic: Temple monks and lamas were capped at three hundred, and weapons were seized for the state.

sentences.zh: 沿江數百里及山谷曠土，招民開墾。

translations.literal: For several hundred li along the river and on vacant land in the valleys, settlers were recruited to open cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: Along hundreds of li of riverbank and on vacant valley land, he recruited settlers to open new fields.

sentences.zh: 舊行滇茶，視打箭爐例，設引收課」。

translations.literal: Yunnan tea was formerly traded; following the precedent of Dajianlu, transit permits were established to collect duties."
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan tea had long been traded there; following the Dajianlu precedent, he established transit permits to collect duties."

sentences.zh: 魯魁山者，自國初為盜藪，夷、倮雜處，推楊、方、普、李四姓為渠。

translations.literal: Lukui Mountain had been a bandit haunt since the founding of the dynasty; Yi and Luo peoples lived intermingled there, and the four surnames Yang, Fang, Pu, and Li were recognized as chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: Lukui Mountain had been a bandit stronghold since the dynasty's founding, with Yi and Luo peoples intermingled; the Yang, Fang, Pu, and Li clans were its recognized leaders.

sentences.zh: 有方景明者，挾倮、夷掠元江。

translations.literal: There was one Fang Jingming, who led Luo and Yi in raiding Yuanjiang.
translations.idiomatic: One Fang Jingming led Luo and Yi raiders against Yuanjiang.

sentences.zh: 其倬遣兵擊破之，擒景明，殲倮、夷數百，疏請於其地駐兵，號普威營。

translations.literal: Qizhuo sent troops to defeat them, captured Jingming, and killed several hundred Luo and Yi; he memorialized requesting a garrison there, to be called the Puwei Camp.
translations.idiomatic: Qizhuo sent troops to rout them, captured Jingming, and killed several hundred Luo and Yi. He memorialized for a garrison there, named the Puwei Camp.

sentences.zh: 參將駐普洱，守備駐威遠、茶山，改威遠歸流，設同知以下官。

translations.literal: A brigade commander was stationed at Pu'er, garrison commanders at Weiyuan and Chashan; Weiyuan was changed to direct administration, and officials down to subprefect were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: A brigade commander was posted at Pu'er and garrison commanders at Weiyuan and Chashan; Weiyuan was brought under direct rule and officials were appointed down to subprefect.

sentences.zh: 土官刁光煥及其孥移置會城，而以新開二鹽井充新設兵餉。

translations.literal: The native official Diao Guanghuan and his family were moved to the provincial capital, and revenue from two newly opened salt wells was assigned to pay the newly established troops.
translations.idiomatic: Native official Diao Guanghuan and his family were relocated to the provincial capital, and two newly opened salt wells were assigned to fund the new garrison.

sentences.zh: 設義塾，教夷人子弟。

translations.literal: Charity schools were established to instruct the sons of tribal peoples.
translations.idiomatic: He set up charity schools to educate tribal youths.

sentences.zh: 元江府學額外增額二名，待其應試。

translations.literal: Two additional examination quotas were added at the Yuanjiang prefectural school, awaiting their candidacy.
translations.idiomatic: Two extra examination places were added at the Yuanjiang prefectural school for them to compete.

sentences.zh: 勸夷人墾田，旱田十年後、水田六年後昇科。

translations.literal: Tribal people were encouraged to reclaim land; dry fields were taxed after ten years, paddy fields after six.
translations.idiomatic: He urged tribal people to open fields, with dry land taxed after ten years and paddy after six.

sentences.zh: 貴州仲家苗酋阿近及其弟阿臥為亂，其倬使撫定傍近諸苗寨。

translations.literal: In Guizhou the Zhongjia Miao chiefs Ajin and his brother Awo rebelled; Qizhuo sent envoys to pacify the neighboring Miao stockades.
translations.idiomatic: In Guizhou the Zhongjia Miao chiefs Ajin and his brother Awo rose in revolt; Qizhuo sent agents to pacify neighboring Miao villages.

sentences.zh: 阿近等失援，遣兵擒戮之，並按治定番、廣順諸苗酋不順命者。

translations.literal: Ajin and the others, deprived of support, were seized and executed by troops he dispatched; he also investigated and punished disobedient Miao chiefs in Dingfan, Guangshun, and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Cut off from support, Ajin and his followers were captured and executed; Qizhuo also punished disobedient Miao chiefs in Dingfan, Guangshun, and other districts.

sentences.zh: 疏請改設定廣協，分置營汛，防定番、廣順及西孟、青藤、斷杉樹、長寨、遮貢、羊城諸地。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting the reorganization of the Dingguang Brigade, with garrisons distributed to defend Dingfan, Guangshun, Ximeng, Qingteng, Duanshan shu, Changzhai, Zhegong, Yangcheng, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to reorganize the Dingguang Brigade and post garrisons to guard Dingfan, Guangshun, Ximeng, Qingteng, Duanshan shu, Changzhai, Zhegong, Yangcheng, and other sites.

sentences.zh: 又移都勻守備駐獨山，改湖廣五開衛為縣，移隸黎平。

translations.literal: He also moved the Duyun garrison commander to Dushan, changed the Huguang Wukai Guard to a county, and transferred its jurisdiction to Liping.
translations.idiomatic: He moved the Duyun garrison commander to Dushan, converted the Huguang Wukai Guard into a county, and placed it under Liping.

sentences.zh: 並言貴州地連川、楚，奸人掠販貧家子女為民害，請飭地方官捕治，歲計人數為課最。

translations.literal: He also stated that Guizhou bordered Sichuan and Huguang, where villains kidnapped and sold the children of poor families to the people's harm, and requested that local officials be ordered to arrest and punish them, with annual counts of persons rescued used to judge merit.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported that Guizhou bordered Sichuan and Huguang, where criminals kidnapped and sold poor people's children. He asked that local officials be ordered to arrest them and that annual rescue counts be used in merit evaluations.

sentences.zh: 貴州民間陋俗，被人劫殺，力不能報，則掠質他家人畜，令轉為報仇；

translations.literal: A vulgar custom in Guizhou was that when one was robbed and killed and lacked strength to retaliate, kin would seize hostages from another household—people or livestock—and compel them to exact vengeance;
translations.idiomatic: A vicious Guizhou custom held that when someone was robbed and killed and the family lacked strength to retaliate, they would seize hostages from another household—people or livestock—and force them to take revenge;

sentences.zh: 不應則索贖，謂之「拏白放黑」。

translations.literal: if they refused, ransom was demanded—this was called "seizing the white and releasing the black."
translations.idiomatic: if they refused, ransom was demanded—a practice called "seizing the white and releasing the black."

sentences.zh: 請加等治罪。

translations.literal: He requested aggravated punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that penalties be increased by one degree.

sentences.zh: 土司貧困，田賦令屬苗代納，請清察，責執業者完賦。

translations.literal: When native chieftains were impoverished, land tax was made the responsibility of subordinate Miao to pay; he requested investigation and that those who actually held the land be required to complete payment.
translations.idiomatic: Impoverished native chieftains often shifted land tax onto subordinate Miao; he asked for an investigation requiring those who actually farmed the land to pay.

sentences.zh: 土司下設權目人等，請令報有司，有罪並懲。

translations.literal: Under native chieftains there were deputies such as quanmu; he requested that they be required to report to the regular officials, and that when guilty they be punished as well.
translations.idiomatic: Deputies such as quanmu served under native chieftains; he asked that they be required to register with civil authorities and be punished when they committed crimes.

sentences.zh: 詔悉如所請。

translations.literal: An edict approved all his requests.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved all his requests.

sentences.zh: 三年，進兵部尚書銜，加太子少傅，調福建浙江總督。

translations.literal: In the third year he was advanced to Minister of War rank, made Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, and transferred as governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he was given Minister of War rank, named Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, and transferred to governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 瀕行，疏言：「鄧川、嵩明、騰越、太和、浪穹諸州縣土軍丁銀，起明嘉靖、萬曆間，遣民防夷，立太和、鳳梧二所，丁徵賦一兩。

translations.literal: On the eve of departure he memorialized: "The native militia service silver of the prefectures and counties of Dengchuan, Songming, Tengyue, Taihe, and Langqiong dates from the Jiajing and Wanli reigns of the Ming, when civilians were dispatched to guard against tribes; the two posts of Taihe and Fengwu were established, and each man was levied one tael.
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving office he memorialized: "The native militia service levy in Dengchuan, Songming, Tengyue, Taihe, Langqiong, and other districts dates from Ming Jiajing and Wanli, when civilians were sent to guard against tribes. The Taihe and Fengwu posts were established, with one tael levied per man.

sentences.zh: 是於本貫已完民賦，請豁除軍糧。

translations.literal: This is in addition to the regular civilian tax already paid in their home districts; I request exemption from the military grain levy."
translations.idiomatic: This is on top of the regular civilian tax already paid in their home districts; I ask that the military grain levy be remitted."

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 四年，疏言：「福、興、漳、泉、汀五府地狹人稠，無田可耕，民且去而為盜。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he memorialized: "The five prefectures of Fu, Xing, Zhang, Quan, and Ting are narrow in land and dense in population; with no fields to till, the people are turning to banditry.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he memorialized: "The five prefectures of Fu, Xing, Zhang, Quan, and Ting are crowded and short of land; with no fields to farm, people are turning to banditry.

sentences.zh: 出海貿易，富者為船主、為商人，貧者為頭舵、為水手，一舟養百人，且得餘利歸贍家屬。

translations.literal: Overseas trade employs the wealthy as ship owners and merchants, the poor as helmsmen and sailors; one vessel supports a hundred men and yields surplus profit to support their families.
translations.idiomatic: Overseas trade lets the wealthy serve as ship owners and merchants and the poor as helmsmen and sailors; one vessel can support a hundred men and still leave profit to support their families.

sentences.zh: 曩者設禁例，如慮盜米出洋，則外洋皆產米地；

translations.literal: Former prohibitions were imposed: if one feared grain being smuggled overseas, foreign seas are all rice-producing regions;
translations.idiomatic: Prohibitions were imposed in the past: if the fear was grain smuggled overseas, foreign seas are themselves rice-producing regions;

sentences.zh: 如慮漏消息，今廣東估舟許出外國，何獨嚴於福建？

translations.literal: if one feared intelligence leaks, Guangdong merchant vessels are now permitted to sail abroad—why should Fujian alone be treated more strictly?
translations.idiomatic: if the fear was intelligence leaks, Guangdong merchant ships are now allowed abroad—why should Fujian alone be treated more harshly?

sentences.zh: 如慮私販船料，中國船小，外國得之不足資其用。

translations.literal: if one feared illicit sale of ship timber, Chinese vessels are small and would be of little use if obtained by foreigners.
translations.idiomatic: If the fear was illicit sale of ship timber, Chinese vessels are small and would be of little use to foreigners even if obtained.

sentences.zh: 臣愚請弛禁便。

translations.literal: Your servant humbly requests that the prohibitions be relaxed for convenience."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant humbly asks that the prohibitions be lifted for the people's benefit."

sentences.zh: 」下怡親王會同大學士九卿議行。

translations.literal: The memorial was referred to Prince Yi, the Grand Secretaries, and the Nine Ministers for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to Prince Yi, the Grand Secretaries, and the Nine Ministers for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 五年，台灣水連社番為亂，其倬遣兵討之，擒其渠骨宗等，諸社悉降。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the Taiwan Shuilian she tribes rebelled; Qizhuo sent troops to suppress them, captured the ringleader Guzong and others, and all the communities submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 the Taiwan Shuilian she tribes rebelled; Qizhuo sent troops to suppress them, captured ringleader Guzong and others, and all the communities surrendered.

sentences.zh: 尋以李衛為浙江總督，命其倬專督福建。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Li Wei was made governor of Zhejiang, and Qizhuo was ordered to supervise Fujian exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Li Wei became governor of Zhejiang, and Qizhuo was ordered to oversee Fujian alone.

sentences.zh: 迭疏請整飭鹽政，改造水師戰船，釐定營汛，並下部議行。

translations.literal: In repeated memorials he requested reform of the salt administration, reconstruction of naval warships, and regulation of garrison posts; these were referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: In repeated memorials he called for salt reform, rebuilding of naval warships, and reorganization of garrison posts; these were sent to the ministries for action.

sentences.zh: 入覲，加太子太保。

translations.literal: On audience at court he was made Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: On presenting himself at court he was named Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 上以其倬通堪輿術，命詣福陵相度。

translations.literal: Because the emperor knew Qizhuo was versed in geomancy, he was ordered to go to the Fuling Mausoleum to survey the site.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Qizhuo was skilled in geomancy, the emperor ordered him to survey the Fuling Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 其倬還奏：「陵前左畔水法，因溢流更故道，弓抱之勢微覺外張。

translations.literal: Qizhuo returned and reported: "The water formation on the left before the mausoleum, because overflow changed the old course, makes the embracing-bow configuration seem slightly outward-flaring.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Qizhuo reported: "The water formation to the left of the mausoleum, because overflow altered the old channel, makes the embracing-bow configuration seem slightly too open.

sentences.zh: 當順導河流，方為盡善。

translations.literal: The river should be guided smoothly—only then will it be fully correct."
translations.idiomatic: The stream should be guided back into a proper course—that would be best."

sentences.zh: 」下大學士等，如所議修濬。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the Grand Secretaries and others, who dredged and repaired as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Secretaries and others carried out dredging and repairs as he proposed.

sentences.zh: 八年，調江南江西總督。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred as governor-general of Jiangnan and Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he was transferred to governor-general of Jiangnan and Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 復召至京師，令從怡親王勘定太平峪萬年吉地，進世職三等阿思哈尼哈番。

translations.literal: He was again summoned to the capital and ordered to join Prince Yi in surveying the auspicious site at Wannian in Taiping Valley; his hereditary office was advanced to third-rank Asihaniha fan.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital to join Prince Yi in selecting the auspicious burial site at Wannian in Taiping Valley, and his hereditary rank was advanced to third-class Asihaniha fan.

sentences.zh: 命署雲貴廣西總督。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve as acting governor-general of Yunnan, Guizhou, and Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed acting governor-general of Yunnan, Guizhou, and Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 十一年，普洱屬思茅土把總刁國興糾苦蔥蠻及元江夷為亂，攻普洱，通關大寨夷复附苦蔥蠻，渡阿墨河攻他郎。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the Simao native company commander Diao Guoxing of Pu'er incited the Kuchong tribes and Yuanjiang Yi to rebel, attacked Pu'er, and the Yi of Tongguan Dazhai again joined the Kuchong, crossed the Amo River, and attacked Talang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 the Simao native company commander Diao Guoxing of Pu'er stirred up the Kuchong tribes and Yuanjiang Yi in revolt, attacked Pu'er, and the Yi of Tongguan Dazhai again sided with the Kuchong, crossed the Amo River, and attacked Talang.

sentences.zh: 其倬檄提督蔡成貴等分道捕治，擒其酋並所屬五百餘，亂乃定。

translations.literal: Qizhuo ordered Provincial Commander Cai Chenggui and others to pursue them by separate routes, captured the chiefs and more than five hundred followers, and the disturbance was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Qizhuo ordered Provincial Commander Cai Chenggui and others to pursue them on separate routes, captured the chiefs and more than five hundred followers, and the rebellion was quelled.

sentences.zh: 是歲春，命其倬回兩江總督。

translations.literal: That spring he was ordered to return as governor-general of the Two Jiangs.
translations.idiomatic: That spring he was ordered back to his post as governor-general of the Two Jiangs.

sentences.zh: 秋，命以總督銜領江蘇巡撫。

translations.literal: In autumn he was ordered to hold the governor-general rank while serving as governor of Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn he was ordered to serve as governor of Jiangsu while retaining governor-general rank.

sentences.zh: 十二年，坐徇知縣趙昆珵償海塘工款，部議降調，即授江蘇巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was impeached for favoring Magistrate Zhao Kunyu in repaying sea-dike project funds; the ministry recommended demotion and transfer, and he was immediately appointed governor of Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 he was censured for favoring Magistrate Zhao Kunyu over repayment of sea-dike funds; though the ministry recommended demotion, he was immediately appointed governor of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，召還京師，复授湖北巡撫，調湖南。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he was recalled to the capital, again appointed governor of Hubei, and transferred to Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 1 he was recalled to the capital, reappointed governor of Hubei, and transferred to Hunan.

sentences.zh: 討平城步、綏寧二縣瑤亂。

translations.literal: He suppressed the Yao rebellions in Chengbu and Suining counties.
translations.idiomatic: He suppressed Yao rebellions in Chengbu and Suining counties.

sentences.zh: 三年，擢工部尚書，調戶部。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted to Minister of Works and transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he was promoted to Minister of Works and transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 其倬詣京師，過寶應，疾作，卒於舟次，賜祭葬，諡文良。

translations.literal: Qizhuo was proceeding to the capital when, passing Baoying, illness seized him and he died aboard his boat; imperial sacrifices and burial were granted, and he was given the posthumous name Wenliang.
translations.idiomatic: While traveling to the capital, Qizhuo fell ill at Baoying and died aboard his boat; the court granted funeral rites and the posthumous name Wenliang.

sentences.zh: 金鉷，字震方，漢軍鑲白旗人，世居登州。

translations.literal: Jin Hong, style name Zhenfang, was a man of the Han military Bordered White Banner whose family had long resided in Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Hong, courtesy name Zhenfang, belonged to the Han military Bordered White Banner; his family had long lived in Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 父延祚，從世祖入關，官至工部侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Yanzuo followed the Shizu Emperor in entering the pass and rose to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yanzuo followed the Shizu Emperor through the pass and rose to Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 鉷初自監生授江西廣昌知縣，洊升山西太原知府。

translations.literal: Hong was first appointed magistrate of Guangchang in Jiangxi from the student registry, and was promoted in due course to prefect of Taiyuan in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Hong first entered service as magistrate of Guangchang, Jiangxi, from the student registry, and was promoted in due course to prefect of Taiyuan, Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 雍正五年，擢廣西按察使，尋遷布政使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongzheng he was promoted to Guangxi provincial judge, and soon transferred to provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 5 he was promoted to Guangxi provincial judge and soon became provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 六年，就擢巡撫。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted directly to governor.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he was promoted directly to governor.

sentences.zh: 討平西隆州八達寨叛苗。

translations.literal: He suppressed the rebellious Miao of the Badazhai stockade in Xilong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He suppressed the rebellious Miao of Badazhai stockade in Xilong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以汛兵少，粵土蕪不治，奏開屯田，與民牛，招之耕，教以技勇。

translations.literal: Because garrison troops were few and Guangdong land lay waste and uncultivated, he memorialized to open military colonies, provide oxen to the people, recruit them to farm, and teach them martial skills.
translations.idiomatic: With too few garrison troops and much Guangdong land lying fallow, he memorialized to open military colonies, provide oxen, recruit farmers, and train them in arms.

sentences.zh: 每名給水田十畝，一畝為公田；

translations.literal: Each man was given ten mu of paddy, one mu as public field;
translations.idiomatic: Each colonist received ten mu of paddy, one mu reserved as public land;

sentences.zh: 旱田二十畝，二畝為公田：存公田租於社倉。

translations.literal: twenty mu of dry land, two mu as public field: public-field rent was kept in the community granary.
translations.idiomatic: or twenty mu of dry land, two mu reserved as public land, with public-field rent stored in the community granary.

sentences.zh: 行之數年，闢田數万畝，倉廩亦實。

translations.literal: After several years of implementation, tens of thousands of mu were opened, and the granaries were also filled.
translations.idiomatic: After several years tens of thousands of mu had been opened and the granaries were full.

sentences.zh: 又奏請召商開桂林屬諸礦，及採梧州金砂供鼓鑄。

translations.literal: He also memorialized requesting merchants be summoned to open the mines under Guilin's jurisdiction and to gather Wuzhou gold sand for coinage.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that merchants be invited to open mines under Guilin and to gather Wuzhou gold sand for minting.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，提督霍升劾鉷言躁氣浮，失封疆大臣之體，高宗召入京，授刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong, Provincial Commander Huo Sheng impeached Hong for impetuous and arrogant speech unbecoming a frontier grandee; the Gaozong Emperor summoned him to the capital and appointed him Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 1 Provincial Commander Huo Sheng impeached Hong for rash, arrogant conduct unbecoming a frontier official; the Gaozong Emperor summoned him to the capital as Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 鉷瀕行，裝不治，以印券囑蒼梧道黃岳牧借銅務充公銀千二百，巡撫楊超曾論劾，奪官，交刑部嚴訊。

translations.literal: On the eve of departure Hong had not settled his luggage accounts and, by sealed warrant, instructed Cangwu Circuit Intendant Huang Yuemu to borrow twelve hundred taels of copper-service funds for public use; Governor Yang Chao impeached him, stripped his office, and referred him to the Ministry of Justice for strict interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving office Hong had not settled his accounts and, by sealed warrant, asked Cangwu Circuit Intendant Huang Yuemu to borrow 1,200 taels from copper-service funds for public use. Governor Yang Chao impeached him, stripped his rank, and sent him to the Ministry of Justice for interrogation.

sentences.zh: 上以非正項錢糧，鉷以印券支借，岳牧以印冊申解，非侵蝕比，命免罪，毋追所借銀。

translations.literal: The emperor held that this was not regular revenue funds: Hong had borrowed on sealed warrant and Yuemu had reported it in the sealed register—not comparable to embezzlement—and ordered exemption from punishment and no recovery of the borrowed silver.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ruled that this was not regular revenue: Hong had borrowed on sealed warrant and Yuemu had reported it properly—not embezzlement—and ordered him pardoned with no recovery of the silver.

sentences.zh: 五年，授河南布政使，而鉷已卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed provincial treasurer of Henan, but Hong had already died.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he was appointed Henan provincial treasurer, but Hong had already died.

sentences.zh: 鉷才通敏。

translations.literal: Hong was talented, quick, and perceptive.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was talented and quick-witted.

sentences.zh: 自太原入覲，方議耗羨歸公，鉷奏曰：「財在上不如在下。

translations.literal: On audience from Taiyuan, when the policy of returning surcharge silver to the public treasury was under discussion, Hong memorialized: "Wealth is better kept below than above.
translations.idiomatic: On presenting himself from Taiyuan, as officials debated returning surcharge silver to the public treasury, Hong argued: "Wealth is better kept below than above.

sentences.zh: 州​​縣親民官，寧使留其有餘，養廉不能胥足，一遇公事，動致侜張。

translations.literal: Prefectural and county magistrates are officials close to the people; it is better to let them retain a surplus. Integrity allowances cannot fully meet their needs; when public business arises, they are driven to irregular expedients."
translations.idiomatic: Prefects and magistrates are the officials closest to the people; it is better to let them keep a surplus. Integrity allowances never fully suffice, and when public business arises they are driven to irregular expedients."

sentences.zh: 上意豈不曰凡是官辦，皆許開支正供？

translations.literal: Does not Your Majesty's intent mean that whatever officials handle may be charged to regular revenue?
translations.idiomatic: Does not Your Majesty intend that all official business may be charged to regular revenue?

sentences.zh: 但從司院按覈以至戶部，層層隔閡，報銷甚難，從此州縣恐多苟且之政。

translations.literal: But from the provincial administration's audit down to the Ministry of Revenue, barriers at every level make reimbursement very difficult; from this the prefectures and counties will likely resort to many perfunctory expedients.
translations.idiomatic: But from provincial audit down to the Ministry of Revenue, barriers at every level make reimbursement very difficult, and prefects and magistrates will likely resort to sloppy shortcuts.

sentences.zh: 上意在必行，臣請養廉外多增公費，或存縣，或存司，庶於事有濟。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's intent must be carried out; your servant requests that beyond integrity allowances additional public-expense funds be added, kept either at the county or at the prefecture, so that affairs may be managed effectively.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty's policy must be carried out, I ask that beyond integrity allowances additional public-expense funds be set aside at county or prefectural level so that affairs can be managed properly.

sentences.zh: 」上乃敕直省覈定公費。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon ordered all provinces to determine public-expense allocations.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered every province to set public-expense allocations.

sentences.zh: 及為廣西布政使，奏請州縣分衝、繁、疲、難四項，許督撫量才奏補，上嘉納之。

translations.literal: When he served as Guangxi provincial treasurer, he memorialized requesting that prefectures and counties be classified into four categories—critical, busy, worn, and difficult—and that governors-general and governors be permitted to recommend appointments according to talent; the emperor commended and adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: As Guangxi provincial treasurer he proposed classifying prefectures and counties into four categories—critical, busy, worn, and difficult—and letting governors recommend appointments by talent; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 州縣缺分四項自此始。

translations.literal: The fourfold classification of prefectural and county posts began from this.
translations.idiomatic: The fourfold classification of prefectural and county posts dates from this proposal.

sentences.zh: 楊宗仁，字天爵，漢軍正白旗人。

translations.literal: Yang Zongren, style name Tianjue, was a man of the Han military Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zongren, courtesy name Tianjue, belonged to the Han military Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 監生。

translations.literal: Student of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service from the Imperial Academy student registry.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十五年，授湖廣慈利知縣。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year of Kangxi he was appointed magistrate of Cili in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 35 he was appointed magistrate of Cili in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 苗酋虐，其眾走縣境，苗酋求之，不與。

translations.literal: A Miao chieftain was cruel; his people fled into the county, and the chieftain demanded them back—Zongren refused.
translations.idiomatic: A Miao chieftain oppressed his people; they fled into the county, and when the chieftain demanded their return, Zongren refused.

sentences.zh: 上官檄與之，宗仁持不可，乃止。

translations.literal: Superiors ordered him to surrender them; Zongren held firm that he could not, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Superiors ordered him to hand them over, but Zongren insisted he could not, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 調藍山。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Lanshan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Lanshan.

sentences.zh: 八排苗為亂，巡撫趙申喬遣兵討之，將不恤兵，兵將為變，宗仁單騎撫定之。

translations.literal: The Bapai Miao rebelled; Governor Zhao Shenqiao sent troops to suppress them, but the generals did not care for the soldiers and the troops were on the verge of mutiny; Zongren went alone on horseback and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Bapai Miao rebelled, Governor Zhao Shenqiao sent troops to suppress them, but the generals neglected the men and a mutiny nearly broke out; Zongren rode out alone and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 舉卓異，四遷甘肅西寧道。

translations.literal: Recommended as outstanding, he was promoted four times to Gansu Xining Circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Rated outstanding in merit review, he was promoted four times to Gansu Xining Circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 五十三年，授浙江按察使，丁父憂歸。

translations.literal: In the fifty-third year he was appointed Zhejiang provincial judge and returned home on his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: In year 53 he was appointed Zhejiang provincial judge and returned home to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，起廣西按察使，署巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year he was recalled as Guangxi provincial judge and served as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: In year 57 he was recalled as Guangxi provincial judge and served as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 旋擢廣東巡撫。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was promoted to governor of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to governor of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 聖祖以各直省錢糧多虧空，諭督撫清理。

translations.literal: Because revenue deficits were widespread in the provinces, the Shenzu Emperor ordered governors-general and governors to clear them up.
translations.idiomatic: Because revenue deficits were widespread across the provinces, the Kangxi Emperor ordered governors to clear them up.

sentences.zh: 宗仁疏言：「廣東虧空現正嚴飭追完。

translations.literal: Zongren memorialized: "Guangdong's deficits are now being strictly pursued to completion.
translations.idiomatic: Zongren memorialized: "Guangdong's deficits are now being strictly pursued to completion.

sentences.zh: 至防杜將來，惟有督撫、司道、府廳交相砥礪，勿藉事勒索。

translations.literal: To guard against the future, governors, provincial officials, and prefectural staffs must encourage one another and must not use any pretext to extort.
translations.idiomatic: To prevent future deficits, governors, circuit officials, and prefectural staffs must hold one another accountable and must not extort under any pretext.

sentences.zh: 州縣正雜錢糧，當責知府不時察覈，毋許虧缺。

translations.literal: Regular and miscellaneous revenues of prefectures and counties should be made the prefect's responsibility to inspect from time to time, with no deficits permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects should be required to inspect prefectural and county revenues regularly and permit no shortfalls.

sentences.zh: 倘敢徇縱，本官治罪，上司從重議處，庶上下皆知儆惕。

translations.literal: If any dare to show favoritism, the official himself shall be punished and his superiors dealt with more severely, so that all levels may know to be vigilant.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who shows favoritism shall be punished, and superiors dealt with more severely, so that all ranks learn vigilance.

sentences.zh: 地方有不得已事，當以督撫等所得公項抵補。

translations.literal: When localities have unavoidable expenses, they should be covered from public funds received by governors and others.
translations.idiomatic: Unavoidable local expenses should be covered from governors' public funds.

sentences.zh: 不敷，則濟以公捐，必不使課帑虛懸。

translations.literal: If insufficient, public contributions should supplement them, and revenue must never be left in deficit."
translations.idiomatic: If that is insufficient, public contributions should supplement it, and revenue must never be left in deficit."

sentences.zh: 」下部議，如所請。

translations.literal: The memorial was referred to the ministries for deliberation and approved as requested.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries deliberated and approved as he requested.

sentences.zh: 六十一年，世宗即位，授湖廣總督。

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year, when the Shizong Emperor acceded, he was appointed governor-general of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 61, upon the Yongzheng Emperor's accession, he was appointed governor-general of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，丁母憂，命在任守制。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he mourned his mother and was ordered to observe mourning while remaining in office.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1 he mourned his mother and was ordered to observe mourning while remaining in office.

sentences.zh: 宗仁疏停本身封廕，為父母求諭祭，許之，仍給封廕。

translations.literal: Zongren memorialized to suspend his own ennoblement for his parents and request imperial sacrifices; this was granted, and the ennoblement was still conferred.
translations.idiomatic: Zongren asked to suspend his own ennoblement to obtain imperial sacrifices for his parents; the request was granted and the ennoblement still conferred.

sentences.zh: 尋賜孔雀翎。

translations.literal: He was soon granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon granted a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「湖廣舊習，文武大吏收受所屬規禮，致州縣橫徵私派，將弁虛兵冒餉，兵民挾比逞私，不敢過問。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "In Huguang the old custom was for civil and military grandees to accept customary gifts from subordinates, leading prefectures and counties to levy arbitrarily and impose private surcharges, officers to pad rolls and draw false pay, and soldiers and civilians to band together for private ends—none dared intervene.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "In Huguang the old custom was for senior civil and military officials to accept gifts from subordinates, leading prefects and magistrates to levy arbitrary surcharges, officers to pad rolls and draw false pay, and soldiers and civilians to band together for private ends with impunity.

sentences.zh: 臣今概行禁革，庶驕兵玩吏錮習潛消。

translations.literal: Your servant now forbids and abolishes all of this entirely, so that the entrenched habits of arrogant troops and negligent officials may quietly disappear."
translations.idiomatic: I have now forbidden all of this, so that the entrenched habits of arrogant troops and negligent officials may fade away."

sentences.zh: 各官貪得鹽規，鹽價增長，民間嗟怨，總督鹽規漸次加至四萬。

translations.literal: Officials greedily took salt surcharges, salt prices rose, and the people groaned in resentment; the governor-general's salt surcharge had gradually reached forty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Officials greedily took salt surcharges, driving up prices and stirring popular resentment; the governor-general's salt surcharge alone had gradually reached forty thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 臣亦行禁革，令商平價以惠窮民。

translations.literal: Your servant has also forbidden and abolished this, ordering merchants to sell at fair prices to benefit the poor.
translations.idiomatic: I have also abolished these practices and ordered merchants to sell at fair prices to benefit the poor.

sentences.zh: 」上深嘉之。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly commended him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor greatly commended him.

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「官有俸，役有工，朝制也。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Officials have salaries and clerks have wages—this is the court's system.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized: "Officials have salaries and clerks have wages—that is the court's system.

sentences.zh: 湖廣州縣以上，俸工報捐已十餘年，官役枵腹，安能禁其不擾民？

translations.literal: In Huguang, for more than ten years prefectures and counties and above have reported salaries and wages as donations; officials and clerks go hungry—how can they be forbidden to harass the people?
translations.idiomatic: In Huguang, for more than ten years prefectural and county salaries and clerks' wages have been reported as donations; officials and clerks go hungry—how can they be stopped from harassing the people?

sentences.zh: 請自雍正元年起，俸工如額編支。

translations.literal: I request that from the first year of Yongzheng salaries and wages be budgeted at full amounts.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that from Yongzheng 1 salaries and wages be budgeted at full amounts.

sentences.zh: 從前有公事，令州縣分捐，實皆轉派於民。

translations.literal: Formerly when there was public business, prefectures and counties were ordered to share donations—in fact all was shifted onto the people.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly public business was funded by levies on prefectures and counties, which in practice were all shifted onto the people.

sentences.zh: 令州縣於加一耗羨內，節省二分，交籓庫充用，此外絲毫不得派捐。

translations.literal: Order prefectures and counties to save two fen from each tael of the ten-percent surcharge and deliver it to the provincial treasury for use; beyond this not a fraction may be levied as donation.
translations.idiomatic: Let prefectures and counties save two fen from each tael of the ten-percent surcharge for the provincial treasury; beyond that not a fraction may be levied.

sentences.zh: 」上諭曰：「所言皆是。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed: "All you say is correct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "All you say is correct.

sentences.zh: 勉之！

translations.literal: Press on!"
translations.idiomatic: Press on!"

sentences.zh: 」尋薦廣東南海知縣宋瑋擢湖南寶慶知府，廣州左衛守備范宗堯改湖北漢陽知縣，上允之，命後勿踵行。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he recommended Nanhai Magistrate Song Wei of Guangdong for promotion to Baqing Prefect in Hunan, and Guangzhou Left Guard Garrison Commander Fan Zongyao for transfer to Hanyang Magistrate in Hubei; the emperor approved but ordered that this not be repeated afterward.
translations.idiomatic: He soon recommended Nanhai Magistrate Song Wei for promotion to Baqing prefect in Hunan and Guangzhou Left Guard Commander Fan Zongyao for transfer to Hanyang magistrate in Hubei; the emperor approved but ordered that such direct recommendations not be repeated.

sentences.zh: 宗仁病作，請以子榆林道文乾自侍，上加文乾按察使銜，馳驛速往，並遣御醫診視。

translations.literal: When Zongren fell ill he asked that his son Yulin Circuit Intendant Wenqian attend him; the emperor added the provincial judge rank to Wenqian, ordered express travel, and sent an imperial physician to examine him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongren fell ill he asked that his son Yulin Circuit Intendant Wenqian attend him; the emperor gave Wenqian provincial judge rank, ordered him to travel post-haste, and sent an imperial physician.

sentences.zh: 宗仁力疾視事，飭諸州縣編保甲，立社倉，罷荊州關私設口岸百五十處。

translations.literal: Zongren forced himself to attend to business despite illness, ordered prefectures and counties to organize baojia, established community granaries, and abolished one hundred fifty privately established checkpoints at Jingzhou Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Despite illness Zongren forced himself to work, ordered prefectures and counties to organize baojia, established community granaries, and abolished 150 private checkpoints at Jingzhou Pass.

sentences.zh: 三年，加太子少傅。

translations.literal: In the third year he was made Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he was named Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，贈少保，予拜他喇布勒哈番世職，賜祭葬，諡清端。

translations.literal: He soon died and was posthumously made Junior Guardian, granted a hereditary Baitalabuleha fan office, given imperial sacrifices and burial, and given the posthumous name Qingduan.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died and was posthumously named Junior Guardian, granted a hereditary Baitalabuleha fan rank, given funeral rites, and posthumously named Qingduan.

sentences.zh: 宗仁砥節矢公，始終一節，上為製像贊，謂「廉潔如冰，耿介如石」。

translations.literal: Zongren honed his integrity and devoted himself to public duty with one consistent principle throughout; the emperor composed an inscription for his portrait, saying he was "pure as ice in integrity, upright as stone in character."
translations.idiomatic: Zongren maintained his integrity throughout; the emperor composed an inscription for his portrait calling him "pure as ice in integrity, upright as stone in character."

sentences.zh: 嘗言：「士當審其所當為，嚴其所不可為。

translations.literal: He once said: "A scholar should discern what he ought to do and be strict about what he must not do."
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "A scholar should discern what he ought to do and be strict about what he must not do."

sentences.zh: 」其馭屬吏寬平忠厚，務安上全下，使各稱其職而止。

translations.literal: In governing subordinates he was lenient, even, and sincere, striving to secure the court above and the people below and to let each fulfill his office and no more.
translations.idiomatic: In governing subordinates he was lenient and sincere, striving to secure the court above and the people below and to let each fulfill his duties and no more.

sentences.zh: 文乾，字元統。

translations.literal: Wenqian, style name Yuantong.
translations.idiomatic: Wenqian, courtesy name Yuantong.

sentences.zh: 以監生效力永定河工。

translations.literal: As a student of the Imperial Academy he served on the Yongding River works.
translations.idiomatic: As an Imperial Academy student he served on the Yongding River works.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十三年，授山東曹州知州，遷東昌知府。

translations.literal: In the fifty-third year of Kangxi he was appointed prefect of Caozhou in Shandong and transferred to Dongchang prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 53 he was appointed prefect of Caozhou, Shandong, and later transferred to Dongchang prefect.

sentences.zh: 舉卓異，遷陝西榆林道。

translations.literal: Recommended as outstanding, he was transferred to Shaanxi Yulin Circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Rated outstanding, he was transferred to Shaanxi Yulin Circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，加按察使銜，命侍宗仁任所。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was given provincial judge rank and ordered to attend Zongren at his post.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1 he was given provincial judge rank and ordered to attend Zongren at his post.

sentences.zh: 三年，宗仁病有間，入謝。

translations.literal: In the third year, when Zongren's illness eased, he went to court to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3, when Zongren's illness eased, he went to court to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 上問湖廣四鎮營製及設鎮始末，文乾具以對，上嘉其詳審，擢河南布政使。

translations.literal: The emperor asked about the organization of Huguang's four garrison towns and the origins of their establishment; Wenqian answered in full detail, and the emperor commended his thoroughness and promoted him to Henan provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked about Huguang's four garrison towns; Wenqian answered in detail, and the emperor commended his thoroughness and promoted him to Henan provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷廣東巡撫，入謝，賜孔雀翎、冠服、鞍馬。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to governor of Guangdong; on audience he was granted a peacock feather, court dress, and saddle horse.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to governor of Guangdong; on presenting himself at court he received a peacock feather, court dress, and saddle horse.

sentences.zh: 宗仁卒，命在任守制。

translations.literal: When Zongren died he was ordered to observe mourning while remaining in office.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongren died he was ordered to observe mourning while remaining in office.

sentences.zh: 廣東省城多盜，文乾令編保甲，以滿洲兵與民連居，會將軍編察，疏聞，上嘉之。

translations.literal: Guangdong's provincial capital had many thieves; Wenqian ordered baojia organized, had Manchu soldiers live among the people, and jointly with the general conducted inspections; he memorialized the throne, which commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong's capital had many thieves; Wenqian organized baojia, had Manchu soldiers live among civilians, and jointly with the general conducted inspections; the emperor commended his memorial.

sentences.zh: 廣東歲歉米貴，文乾令吏詣廣西買穀平糶。

translations.literal: Guangdong had a lean year and costly rice; Wenqian ordered clerks to go to Guangxi to buy grain and sell it at fair prices.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangdong suffered a poor harvest and rice prices soared, Wenqian sent clerks to Guangxi to buy grain and sell it at fair prices.

sentences.zh: 滿洲兵閻尚義等群聚掠穀，文乾令捕治。

translations.literal: Manchu soldiers Yan Shangyi and others gathered in bands to plunder grain; Wenqian ordered their arrest and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Manchu soldiers led by Yan Shangyi gathered in bands to plunder grain; Wenqian ordered their arrest.

sentences.zh: 將軍李枚庇兵，文乾請遣大臣按治。

translations.literal: General Li Mei shielded the soldiers; Wenqian requested that a high minister be sent to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: General Li Mei shielded the soldiers; Wenqian asked that a high minister be sent to investigate.

sentences.zh: 上命侍郎塞楞額、阿克敦往勘，枚及尚義等論罪如律。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Vice Ministers Sailenge and Akedun to go investigate; Li Mei, Yan Shangyi, and others were sentenced according to law.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Vice Ministers Sailenge and Akedun to investigate; Li Mei, Yan Shangyi, and others were sentenced according to law.

sentences.zh: 文乾蒞政精勤，多所釐正。

translations.literal: Wenqian was diligent and exacting in administration and corrected many abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Wenqian administered with diligence and corrected many abuses.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「廣東民納糧多用老戶，臣令改立的名，杜​​詭寄、飛灑諸弊，民以為便。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Guangdong people mostly paid grain tax through old household registers; your servant ordered registration under actual names, stopping abuses such as false registration and scattered assessment, to the people's convenience.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Guangdong taxpayers mostly paid through old household registers; I ordered registration under actual names, stopping false registration and scattered assessment abuses, to the people's benefit.

sentences.zh: 丁銀隨糧辦者十四五，餘令布政使確核，盡歸地糧。

translations.literal: Only fourteen or fifteen in a hundred of poll-tax silver was collected with grain tax; the remainder I order the provincial treasurer to verify strictly and merge entirely into land tax."
translations.idiomatic: Only about fourteen or fifteen percent of poll tax was collected with grain tax; I order the provincial treasurer to verify the remainder and merge it entirely into land tax."

sentences.zh: 」得旨嘉獎。

translations.literal: An imperial rescript commended him.
translations.idiomatic: The throne commended him.

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「廣東地狹人眾，現存倉穀一百六十餘萬石，為民食久遠計，應加貯二百餘萬石，擇地建倉貯穀。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Guangdong is narrow in land and dense in population; granaries now hold more than 1.6 million shi; for the people's long-term food supply an additional 2 million-plus shi should be stored, with sites chosen to build granaries."
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized: "Guangdong is crowded and short of land; granaries now hold more than 1.6 million shi. For long-term food security an additional 2 million shi should be stored in new granaries."

sentences.zh: 」下廷議，令於海陽、潮陽、程鄉、饒平、海豐、瓊山加貯穀三十四萬石，從之。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to court deliberation, which ordered an additional 340,000 shi stored in Haiyang, Chaoyang, Chengxiang, Raoping, Haifeng, and Qiongshan; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Court deliberation ordered an additional 340,000 shi stored in Haiyang, Chaoyang, Chengxiang, Raoping, Haifeng, and Qiongshan, and this was approved.

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「廣東公使銀歲六七萬，取諸火耗。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Guangdong's public-service silver amounts to sixty or seventy thousand a year, drawn from meltage.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized: "Guangdong's public-service funds amount to sixty or seventy thousand taels a year, drawn from meltage.

sentences.zh: 臣為裁省，歲計需四萬餘。

translations.literal: Your servant has cut expenses; the annual need is a little over forty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: I have cut expenses to a little over forty thousand taels a year.

sentences.zh: 擬以民間置產推糧易戶例納公費及屯糧陋規兩項充用。

translations.literal: It is proposed to cover this from two sources: the customary public fee when common people register property and shift tax liability, and corrupt practices in garrison grain.
translations.idiomatic: I propose funding this from fees on property transfers and tax reassessments and from abolishing corrupt garrison-grain practices.

sentences.zh: 州縣火耗，每兩加一，實計一錢三四分有奇，十之五六留充州縣養廉，十之七八為督撫以下各官養廉。

translations.literal: Prefectural and county meltage, nominally ten percent per tael, actually amounts to one mace and three or four fen odd; five or six tenths remain for prefectural and county integrity allowances, seven or eight tenths for integrity allowances of governors and officials below them.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural and county meltage, nominally ten percent per tael, actually comes to about one mace and three or four fen; five or six tenths fund local integrity allowances and seven or eight tenths fund allowances for governors and subordinates.

sentences.zh: 」上諭之曰：「但務得中為是。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed him: "Only seek the mean—that is right.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor instructed him: "Only seek the balanced course.

sentences.zh: 民不可令驕慢，屬吏亦不可令窘乏。

translations.literal: The people must not be allowed to grow arrogant, but subordinates must not be left in want either.
translations.idiomatic: The people must not be allowed to grow arrogant, but subordinates must not be left destitute either.

sentences.zh: 天下事惟貴平，當徹始終籌畫，慎毋輕舉。

translations.literal: In all affairs under heaven balance is prized; plan thoroughly from start to finish and do not act rashly."
translations.idiomatic: In all affairs balance is what matters; plan thoroughly from start to finish and do not act rashly."

translations.literal: " (end of imperial instruction)
translations.idiomatic: " (end of imperial instruction)

sentences.zh: 五年，乞假葬父。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he requested leave to bury his father.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he requested leave to bury his father.

sentences.zh: 福建巡撫常賚劾文乾徵粵海關稅，設專行六，得銀二十餘萬；

translations.literal: Fujian Governor Chang Gai impeached Wenqian for collecting Guangdong maritime customs duties, establishing six exclusive agents, and obtaining more than two hundred thousand taels of silver;
translations.idiomatic: Fujian Governor Chang Gai impeached Wenqian for collecting Guangdong maritime customs duties through six exclusive agents and obtaining more than two hundred thousand taels;

sentences.zh: 又疏劾文乾匿粵海關羨餘銀五萬餘，縱綢緞出洋，得銀萬餘，番銀加一扣收，得銀四萬餘，選洋船奇巧之物入署，令專行代償，又銀二萬餘，又以銀交鹽商營運。

translations.literal: he also impeached Wenqian for concealing more than fifty thousand taels of Guangdong customs surplus, allowing silk and satin to go overseas for more than ten thousand taels, taking an extra ten percent on foreign silver for more than forty thousand, selecting curious goods from foreign ships for his yamen and having agents pay for them for another twenty thousand-plus, and lending silver to salt merchants for profit.
translations.idiomatic: he also accused Wenqian of concealing more than fifty thousand taels of customs surplus, allowing silk to be exported for over ten thousand taels, taking an extra ten percent on foreign silver for over forty thousand, having agents pay for curios from foreign ships for another twenty thousand-plus, and lending silver to salt merchants for profit.

sentences.zh: 上嚴諭文乾，令愧悔痛改。

translations.literal: The emperor sternly admonished Wenqian to repent and reform thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sternly admonished Wenqian to repent and reform thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 尋以福建倉庫虧空，命文乾與浙江觀風整俗使許容等往按，而移常賚署廣東巡撫。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, because Fujian's granaries were in deficit, Wenqian was ordered to investigate jointly with Zhejiang Commissioner for Customs and Morals Xu Rong and others, while Chang Gai was transferred to act as Guangdong governor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, because Fujian's granaries were in deficit, Wenqian was ordered to investigate with Zhejiang Commissioner Xu Rong and others, while Chang Gai was transferred to act as Guangdong governor.

sentences.zh: 文乾令分路察核官虧民欠，分別追納，不敷，責前巡撫毛文銓償補。

translations.literal: Wenqian ordered investigations by separate routes into official deficits and popular arrears, recovery according to category, and where insufficient, held former Governor Mao Wenquan responsible to make up the shortfall.
translations.idiomatic: Wenqian ordered separate investigations into official deficits and popular arrears, recovery by category, and where funds fell short held former Governor Mao Wenquan responsible to make up the difference.

sentences.zh: 上獎文乾秉公無瞻顧。

translations.literal: The emperor praised Wenqian for acting impartially without regard to personal considerations.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised Wenqian for acting impartially without favoritism.

sentences.zh: 文乾疏言：「福建府、州、縣各官都計八十員，前後劾罷五十餘員。

translations.literal: Wenqian memorialized: "Fujian's prefectural and county officials number eighty in all; more than fifty have been impeached and removed before and after.
translations.idiomatic: Wenqian memorialized: "Fujian has eighty prefectural and county officials in all; more than fifty have been impeached and removed.

sentences.zh: 新補各官，守倉庫有餘，理繁劇不足。

translations.literal: The newly appointed officials are adequate for guarding granaries but insufficient for handling busy and difficult affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The newly appointed officials can guard granaries but lack capacity for busy, difficult posts.

sentences.zh: 請選熟諳民事者，詣福建補繁要州縣。

translations.literal: I request that those well versed in civil affairs be selected and sent to Fujian to fill busy and important prefectures and counties."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that officials well versed in civil affairs be selected and sent to Fujian for busy, important prefectural and county posts."

sentences.zh: 」上為敕各督撫各選謹慎敏練之吏諮送福建。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon ordered each governor-general and governor to select careful, capable officials and recommend them to Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered every governor to select careful, capable officials and recommend them to Fujian.

sentences.zh: 文乾強幹善折獄。

translations.literal: Wenqian was forceful and skilled at deciding cases.
translations.idiomatic: Wenqian was forceful and skilled at deciding cases.

sentences.zh: 初知曹州，有婦告夫為人殺者。

translations.literal: When he first served as Caozhou prefect, a woman reported that her husband had been killed by someone.
translations.idiomatic: When he first served as Caozhou prefect, a woman reported that her husband had been murdered.

sentences.zh: 文乾視其屨白，問曰：「若夫死，若預知之乎？

translations.literal: Wenqian noticed her shoes were white and asked: "If your husband died, did you know beforehand?
translations.idiomatic: Wenqian noticed her shoes were white and asked: "If your husband died, did you know beforehand?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「今旦乃知之。

translations.literal: She said: "I only learned of it this morning."
translations.idiomatic: She said: "I only learned of it this morning."

sentences.zh: 」曰：「然則汝何辦白屨之夙也？

translations.literal: He said: "Then why did you prepare white shoes so long ago?"
translations.idiomatic: He said: "Then why did you prepare white mourning shoes so long ago?"

sentences.zh: 」婦乃服以姦殺夫。

translations.literal: The woman then confessed to adultery and killing her husband.
translations.idiomatic: The woman then confessed to adultery and murdering her husband.

sentences.zh: 五人者同宿，其一失金，訟其四，文乾令坐於庭，視久之，曰：「吾已得盜金者，非盜聽去。

translations.literal: Five men lodged together; one lost gold and sued the other four. Wenqian had them sit in the court, watched a long while, and said: "I have found the thief of the gold; those who did not steal may leave.
translations.idiomatic: Five men lodged together; one lost gold and accused the other four. Wenqian had them sit in court, watched a long while, and said: "I have found the thief; those who did not steal may leave.

sentences.zh: 」一人欲起，執之，果盜金者。

translations.literal: One man started to rise; Wenqian seized him, and he proved to be the thief of the gold.
translations.idiomatic: One man started to rise; Wenqian seized him, and he proved to be the thief.

sentences.zh: 曹民有偽稱硃六太子者，挾妖術惑愚民，朝命侍郎勒什布、湯右曾按治。

translations.literal: A man of Caozhou falsely called himself the Vermilion Sixth Prince and used sorcery to delude the foolish populace; the court ordered Vice Ministers Leshibu and Tang Youzeng to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: A Caozhou man falsely called himself the Vermilion Sixth Prince and used sorcery to delude the people; the court ordered Vice Ministers Leshibu and Tang Youzeng to investigate.

sentences.zh: 檄至，文乾秘之，密捕得送京師。

translations.literal: When the order arrived, Wenqian kept it secret, secretly captured the man, and sent him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the order arrived, Wenqian kept it secret, secretly captured the impostor, and sent him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 在東昌，請運糧饋軍出西寧，先期至，以是受知於世宗。

translations.literal: At Dongchang he requested to transport grain to supply the army in Xining and arrived ahead of schedule; thereby he won the Shizong Emperor's notice.
translations.idiomatic: At Dongchang he volunteered to transport grain to supply the army in Xining and arrived ahead of schedule, thereby winning the Yongzheng Emperor's notice.

sentences.zh: 然頗與同官多齟《齒吾》。

translations.literal: Yet he had much friction with colleagues.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he had much friction with colleagues.

sentences.zh: 赴廣東，途中疏劾布政使硃絳倚總督孔毓珣有連，虧帑三萬餘。

translations.literal: On his way to Guangdong he memorialized impeaching Provincial Treasurer Zhu Jiang, who relied on connections with Governor-General Kong Yuxun and had a treasury deficit of more than thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On his way to Guangdong he impeached Provincial Treasurer Zhu Jiang, who relied on ties to Governor-General Kong Yuxun and had embezzled more than thirty thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 毓珣疏先入，上命文乾毋聽屬吏離間。

translations.literal: Kong Yuxun's memorial arrived first; the emperor ordered Wenqian not to heed subordinates' attempts to sow division.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yuxun's memorial arrived first; the emperor ordered Wenqian not to heed subordinates' attempts to sow division.

sentences.zh: 既上官，疏言盜案塵積，請概為速結。

translations.literal: After taking office he memorialized that theft cases had piled up like dust and requested that they all be concluded quickly.
translations.idiomatic: After taking office he reported that theft cases had piled up and asked that they all be concluded quickly.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「孔毓珣緝捕盜賊甚盡力。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed: "Kong Yuxun has exerted himself greatly in arresting bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Kong Yuxun has worked hard to arrest bandits.

sentences.zh: 彼擒之，汝縱之，恐汝不能當此論。

translations.literal: He captures them and you release them—I fear you cannot bear this criticism.
translations.idiomatic: He captures them and you release them—I fear you cannot answer for that.

sentences.zh: 縱虎歸山，豈為仁政？

translations.literal: To release a tiger back to the mountains—is that benevolent government?
translations.idiomatic: To release a tiger back to the mountains—is that benevolent government?

sentences.zh: 宜加意斟酌。

translations.literal: You should deliberate with extra care.
translations.idiomatic: You should deliberate with extra care.

sentences.zh: 」在福建，毓珣入覲，上命侍郎阿克敦署兩廣總督。

translations.literal: In Fujian, when Kong Yuxun went to audience, the emperor ordered Vice Minister Akedun to serve as acting governor-general of the Two Guangs.
translations.idiomatic: In Fujian, when Kong Yuxun went to court, the emperor ordered Vice Minister Akedun to serve as acting governor-general of the Two Guangs.

sentences.zh: 文乾疏言盜劫龍門營軍器，阿克敦令從寬結案；

translations.literal: Wenqian memorialized that bandits had robbed military equipment from Longmen Camp and Akedun ordered the case closed leniently;
translations.idiomatic: Wenqian reported that bandits had robbed military equipment from Longmen Camp and that Akedun had ordered the case closed leniently;

sentences.zh: 將軍標兵窩盜，將軍石禮哈袒兵，謂告者誣良。

translations.literal: The general's banner troops harbored thieves; General Shi Liha shielded his troops and declared the accuser was slandering good men.
translations.idiomatic: The general's banner troops were harboring thieves; General Shi Liha shielded his men and claimed the accuser had falsely implicated the innocent.

sentences.zh: 既，上命常賚還福建，而以阿克敦署廣東巡撫。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, the emperor ordered Chang Gui back to Fujian and appointed Akedun acting governor of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, the emperor ordered Chang Gui back to Fujian and made Akedun acting governor of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 六年，文乾還廣東，劾阿克敦勒索暹羅商船規禮，布政使官達縱幕客納賄，皆奪官。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Wenqian returned to Guangdong and impeached Akedun for extorting customary gifts from Siamese merchant vessels and Guan Da, the provincial treasurer, for allowing his staff to accept bribes; all were stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, Wenqian returned to Guangdong and impeached Akedun for extorting gifts from Siamese merchant ships and Provincial Treasurer Guan Da for letting his staff accept bribes; all were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 命文乾與毓珣會鞫，未及訊，文乾卒，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Wenqian and Kong Yuxun to conduct a joint investigation; before the inquiry could be held, Wenqian died and was granted funeral sacrifices and burial honors.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Wenqian and Kong Yuxun to investigate jointly, but Wenqian died before the inquiry could begin and was granted funeral rites and burial honors.

sentences.zh: 子應琚，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Yingju has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yingju has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 孔毓珣，字東美，山東曲阜人，孔子六十六世孫。

translations.literal: Kong Yuxun, styled Dongmei, was a native of Qufu in Shandong and the sixty-sixth-generation descendant of Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yuxun, styled Dongmei, was a native of Qufu in Shandong and a sixty-sixth-generation descendant of Confucius.

sentences.zh: 父恩洪，福建按察使。

translations.literal: His father, Enhong, served as provincial surveillance commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: His father Enhong had served as provincial surveillance commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十三年，上幸曲阜釋奠，毓珣以諸生陪祀，賜恩貢生。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Kangxi, when the emperor visited Qufu to perform the sacrificial rites, Yuxun, as a student, participated in the ceremony and was granted the status of enriched gongshi.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 23, when the emperor visited Qufu for the sacrificial rites, Yuxun participated as a student and was granted the status of enriched gongshi.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，授湖廣武昌通判。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, he was appointed sub-prefect of Wuchang in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he was appointed sub-prefect of Wuchang in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 舉卓異，遷江南徐州知州。

translations.literal: Nominated as outstanding, he was transferred to serve as prefect of Xuzhou in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: After being rated outstanding, he was transferred to serve as prefect of Xuzhou in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 徐州民敝於丁賦，毓珣在官七年，拊循多惠政。

translations.literal: The people of Xuzhou were exhausted by poll taxes and corvée levies; Yuxun served there seven years, soothing them with many benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Xuzhou were worn down by poll taxes and corvée; Yuxun served seven years there, governing with many compassionate measures.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，河道總督張鵬翮以毓珣熟於河務，薦授邳睢同知。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year, Zhang Penghe, director-general of river works, recommended Yuxun for his expertise in river affairs, and he was appointed sub-prefect of Pi and Sui.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year, River Works Director-General Zhang Penghe recommended Yuxun for his expertise in river management, and he was appointed sub-prefect of Pi and Sui.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，遷山西平陽知府，未上，改雲南順寧。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year, he was transferred to serve as prefect of Pingyang in Shanxi; before taking up the post, he was reassigned to Shunning in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year he was transferred to prefect of Pingyang in Shanxi, but before he could take up the post he was reassigned to Shunning in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，調開化，以母憂去官。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year, he was transferred to Kaihua but left office upon his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year he was transferred to Kaihua but resigned when his mother died.

sentences.zh: 五十年，服終，除四川龍安。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year, when mourning was complete, he was appointed to Long'an in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fiftieth year, after mourning ended, he was appointed to Long'an in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 毓珣歷守邊郡，皆因俗為治，弊去其太甚，邊民安之。

translations.literal: Yuxun successively governed frontier prefectures, tailoring governance to local custom, removing the worst abuses without overreach; the border people lived in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive frontier posts, Yuxun governed according to local custom, removing the worst abuses without going too far, and the border people lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 再舉卓異。

translations.literal: He was again nominated as outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: He was again rated outstanding.

sentences.zh: 五十五年，遷湖廣上荊南道。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year, he was transferred to Upper Jingnan Circuit in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fifth year he was transferred to Upper Jingnan Circuit in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 築堤捍江，民號曰孔公堤。

translations.literal: He built dikes to hold back the river; the people called them Prefect Kong's Dike.
translations.idiomatic: He built dikes to hold back the river, and the people called them Prefect Kong's Dike.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，遷廣西按察使。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year, he was made provincial surveillance commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-sixth year he became provincial surveillance commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 廣西地瘠民悍，瑤、僮為民害。

translations.literal: Guangxi's land was poor and its people fierce; the Yao and Zhuang were a bane to the populace.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi was poor and its people fierce; the Yao and Zhuang plagued the common folk.

sentences.zh: 靈川僮酋廖三屢出焚掠，毓珣白巡撫陳元龍，遣兵捕得置諸法，諸苗讋服。

translations.literal: The Zhuang chieftain Liao San of Lingchuan repeatedly led raids of burning and plunder; Yuxun informed Governor Chen Yuanlong, dispatched troops to capture him and punish him by law, and the various tribes submitted in awe.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhuang chieftain Liao San of Lingchuan repeatedly raided and plundered; Yuxun informed Governor Chen Yuanlong, sent troops to capture him and punish him by law, and the tribes submitted in awe.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，授四川布政使。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year, he was appointed provincial administration commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-seventh year he was appointed provincial administration commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 西藏方用兵，毓珣轉餉出察木多，不以勞民。

translations.literal: Tibet was at war; Yuxun transported supplies through Qamdo without overburdening the people.
translations.idiomatic: While Tibet was at war, Yuxun transported supplies through Qamdo without overburdening the populace.

sentences.zh: 重築灌江口堰，四川民尤德之。

translations.literal: He rebuilt the weir at Guanjiangkou, for which the people of Sichuan were especially grateful.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt the weir at Guanjiangkou, earning special gratitude from the people of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 六十一年，擢廣西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year, he was promoted to governor of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixty-first year he was promoted to governor of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，加授總督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng, he was additionally appointed governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1 he was additionally made governor-general.

sentences.zh: 廣西提鎮標空糧，毓珣飭募補。

translations.literal: Vacant grain rations in the Guangxi provincial and garrison banner units—Yuxun ordered recruitment to fill them.
translations.idiomatic: Grain rations in Guangxi's provincial and garrison banner units had empty places on the rolls; Yuxun ordered recruitment to fill the gaps.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「各官俸不足自贍，請於定例外量加親丁名糧。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Officials' salaries are insufficient for self-support; I request that household grain allowances beyond the fixed quota be added in moderate measure.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Official salaries are insufficient for self-support; I ask that household grain allowances beyond the fixed quota be modestly increased.

sentences.zh: 」上命酌中為之。

translations.literal: " The emperor ordered a moderate adjustment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered a moderate adjustment.

sentences.zh: 廣西諸州縣舊有常平倉，毓珣議：「春耕借於民，秋收還倉，年豐加息，歉免息，荒緩至次年還本。

translations.literal: Guangxi's prefectures and counties had permanent granaries; Yuxun proposed: "At spring plowing, lend grain to the people; at autumn harvest, return it to the granary. In good years add interest; in poor years waive interest; in famine years defer principal repayment until the following year.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi's prefectures and counties maintained permanent granaries; Yuxun proposed: "Lend to the people at spring plowing and return the grain at autumn harvest. Charge interest in good years, waive it in lean years, and in famine defer principal repayment to the following year.

sentences.zh: 日久穀多，分貯四鄉，建社倉，擇里中信實者為司出入。

translations.literal: Over time grain accumulates; distribute it to storage in the four townships, build community granaries, and select trustworthy village elders to manage receipts and disbursements.
translations.idiomatic: As grain accumulates over time, distribute it to storage sites in the countryside, establish community granaries, and appoint trustworthy village elders to manage receipts and disbursements.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「地多盜，瑤、僮雜處，保甲不能遍立。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Banditry is widespread; Yao and Zhuang live intermixed, and the baojia system cannot be fully established everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: "He also said: "Banditry is widespread, and with Yao and Zhuang living intermixed, the baojia system cannot be established everywhere.

sentences.zh: 諸鄉多有團練，令選誠幹者充鄉勇，得盜者賞，怠惰者罰。

translations.literal: Many townships already have militia corps; select capable men to serve as village braves, reward those who capture bandits and punish the idle.
translations.idiomatic: Many townships already have militia; let capable men serve as village braves, reward captures, and punish neglect.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「廣西邊遠，鹽商多滯運，民憂淡食。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Guangxi is remote; salt merchants often delay delivery, and the people fear a shortage of salt.
translations.idiomatic: "He also said: "Guangxi is remote; salt merchants often delay shipments, and the people worry about running out of salt.

sentences.zh: 請發籓庫銀六萬，官為運銷。

translations.literal: I request six hundred thousand taels from the provincial treasury to transport and sell salt under official auspices.
translations.idiomatic: I request six hundred thousand taels from the provincial treasury for official transport and sale of salt.

sentences.zh: 行有贏餘，本還籓庫，並可量減鹽價。
