translations.literal: Any surplus from operations shall return principal to the provincial treasury and can also be used to reduce salt prices moderately.
translations.idiomatic: Any surplus would return the principal to the provincial treasury and could also be used to reduce salt prices.

sentences.zh: 」並從之。

translations.literal: " All proposals were approved.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 柳州僮莫貴鳳出掠馬平、柳城、永福諸縣，毓珣遣兵捕治，毀其寨，置貴鳳於法。

translations.literal: The Zhuang Mo Guifeng raided Maping, Liucheng, Yongfu, and other counties; Yuxun dispatched troops to capture and punish him, destroyed his stockade, and executed Guifeng by law.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhuang leader Mo Guifeng raided Maping, Liucheng, Yongfu, and other counties; Yuxun sent troops to capture him, destroyed his stockade, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 來賓僮覃扶成等出掠，未傷人，毓珣令予杖荷校，滿日，充撫標兵，散其黨類。

translations.literal: The Zhuang Tan Fucheng and others of Laibin raided without harming anyone; Yuxun ordered them beaten with the cangue, and after the term expired, enrolled them as garrison banner troops and dispersed their followers.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhuang Tan Fucheng and others from Laibin had raided but harmed no one; Yuxun had them beaten and placed in the cangue, then after their term enrolled them in the governor's banner troops and dispersed their followers.

sentences.zh: 疏聞，上嘉其寬嚴兩得。

translations.literal: When the memorial was received, the emperor praised his balance of leniency and severity.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the emperor praised his balance of leniency and severity.

sentences.zh: 二年，授兩廣總督。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was appointed governor-general of the Two Guangs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed governor-general of the Two Guangs.

sentences.zh: 上諭之曰：「廣東武備廢弛，劫掠公行，舉劾官吏，百無一公，爾當盡心料理。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed him: "Guangdong's defenses are lax, robbery runs rampant, and memorials impeaching officials are rarely fair—you must exert yourself in managing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him: "Guangdong's defenses are in disrepair, robbery is rampant, and impeachments of officials are rarely impartial—you must give the matter your full attention.

sentences.zh: 」毓珣疏請釐定鹽政，灶丁鹽價、船戶水腳增十之一，並免埠商羨餘；

translations.literal: Yuxun memorialized requesting reform of the salt administration, raising salt worker prices and boatmen freight rates by one tenth, and exempting port merchants' surplus levies;
translations.idiomatic: Yuxun memorialized to reform salt administration, raise prices for salt workers and freight rates for boatmen by one tenth, and abolish surplus levies on port merchants;

sentences.zh: 設潮州運同、鹽運司經歷。

translations.literal: establish the posts of Chaozhou transport intendant and salt transport bureau registrar.
translations.idiomatic: he also proposed establishing the posts of Chaozhou transport intendant and salt transport bureau registrar.

sentences.zh: 大金、蕉木兩山產礦砂，東隸開建、連山，西隸賀縣、懷集。

translations.literal: Dajin and Jiaomu mountains produce ore sand; the east belongs to Kaijian and Lianshan, the west to Hexian and Huaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Dajin and Jiaomu mountains produce ore sand; the eastern slopes lie in Kaijian and Lianshan, the western in Hexian and Huaiji.

sentences.zh: 舊制，懷集汛屬潯州協，毓珣請改屬梧州協，賀縣、開建、連山並增兵設汛。

translations.literal: Under the old system, the Huaiji garrison post belonged to Xunzhou Command; Yuxun requested transferring it to Wuzhou Command and adding garrison troops and posts at Hexian, Kaijian, and Lianshan.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system the Huaiji garrison came under Xunzhou Command; Yuxun asked to transfer it to Wuzhou Command and add garrison troops and posts at Hexian, Kaijian, and Lianshan.

sentences.zh: 廣東香山澳西洋商舶，毓珣請以二十五艘為限。

translations.literal: Western merchant vessels at Xiangshan Ao in Guangdong—Yuxun requested limiting them to twenty-five ships.
translations.idiomatic: For Western merchant vessels at Xiangshan Ao in Guangdong, Yuxun asked to cap their number at twenty-five.

sentences.zh: 皆下部議行。

translations.literal: All were referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: All were referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.

sentences.zh: 潮州田少米貴，民賴常平倉穀以濟。

translations.literal: Chaozhou has little farmland and dear rice; the people rely on permanent granary grain for relief.
translations.idiomatic: Chaozhou has little farmland and expensive rice; the people depend on permanent granary grain for relief.

sentences.zh: 毓珣請提鎮各營貯穀借兵，散餉時買還，概免加息，上特允之。

translations.literal: Yuxun requested that each garrison camp store grain for lending to troops, to be repurchased when pay was disbursed, with all interest waived; the emperor specially approved this.
translations.idiomatic: Yuxun asked that each garrison camp store grain to lend to troops, to be repurchased when pay was issued, with all interest waived; the emperor approved this specially.

sentences.zh: 三年，加兵部尚書銜。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was granted the honorary rank of minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was granted the honorary rank of minister of war.

sentences.zh: 四年，毓珣請入覲，上以毓珣習河事，令詳勘黃、運諸河水勢，協同齊蘇勒酌議。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Yuxun requested an audience; because Yuxun was versed in river affairs, the emperor ordered him to inspect in detail the water conditions of the Yellow and Transport rivers and consult with Qi Sule.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Yuxun requested an audience; recognizing his expertise in river affairs, the emperor ordered him to inspect the Yellow and Grand Canal rivers in detail and confer with Qi Sule.

sentences.zh: 毓珣疏言：「宿遷縣西，黃河與中河相近，舊有汰黃壩。

translations.literal: Yuxun memorialized: "West of Suqian County, the Yellow River and Middle River lie close; there was formerly a sluice to drain Yellow River water.
translations.idiomatic: Yuxun reported: "West of Suqian County the Yellow River and Middle River run close together; there was once a sluice to drain Yellow River water.

sentences.zh: 運河水大，引清水刷黃，黃河水大，引黃水濟運。

translations.literal: When the canal water was high, clear water was drawn to scour the Yellow; when Yellow River water was high, Yellow River water was drawn to supply the canal.
translations.idiomatic: When canal water ran high, clear water was diverted to scour the Yellow River channel; when the Yellow River ran high, its water was diverted to supply the canal.

sentences.zh: 舊時黃水入中河不過十之一二，今河南岸沙漲，逼水北行，水流甚急。

translations.literal: Formerly Yellow River water entering the Middle River was no more than one or two tenths; now sand has built up on the Henan south bank, forcing the water northward, and the current is very swift.
translations.idiomatic: Previously only a tenth or two of Yellow River water entered the Middle River; now sand has built up on the Henan south bank, forcing the water northward and making the current very swift.

sentences.zh: 齊蘇勒議收小汰黃壩口以束水勢。

translations.literal: Qi Sule proposed narrowing the sluice mouth to restrain the water's force.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Sule proposed narrowing the sluice mouth to constrain the water's force.

sentences.zh: 臣詳勘南岸漲沙曲處，宜濬引河以避此險。

translations.literal: Your servant, having inspected in detail the sand buildup along the south bank's curves, believes a diversion channel should be dredged to avoid this danger.
translations.idiomatic: After inspecting the sand buildup along the south bank's bends, I believe a diversion channel should be dredged to avoid this hazard.

sentences.zh: 仍俟齊蘇勒相度定議。

translations.literal: I await Qi Sule's on-site survey for a final decision.
translations.idiomatic: I await Qi Sule's on-site survey before a final decision.

sentences.zh: 」又陳江南水利，言：「吳淞、劉河、七浦、白茆諸閘，宜令管閘官役隨潮啟閉。

translations.literal: " He also addressed Jiangnan water works, saying: "The sluices at Wusong, Liu River, Qipu, and Baimao should have their managing officials open and close them according to the tides.
translations.idiomatic: "He also addressed Jiangnan water works: "The sluices at Wusong, Liu River, Qipu, and Baimao should be opened and closed with the tides by the officials in charge.

sentences.zh: 江蘇地形四高中下，宜令力勸築區立圩。

translations.literal: Jiangsu's terrain is high on four sides and low in the center; the people should be vigorously encouraged to build polder fields and dikes.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangsu's terrain is high on four sides and low in the center; officials should vigorously encourage polder construction.

sentences.zh: 濱河諸地民佔為田廬，其無甚害者，姑從民便，餘宜嚴禁。

translations.literal: Where people along the rivers have encroached to build fields and dwellings, if no serious harm is done, provisionally accommodate the people's convenience; the rest should be strictly forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Where people along the rivers have encroached to farm and build, cases of little harm may be tolerated for the people's convenience; the rest should be strictly prohibited.

sentences.zh: 支河小港，宜令於農隙深濬，即取土培圩。

translations.literal: Branch rivers and small channels should be deeply dredged during farming slack season, using the excavated earth to heighten the dikes.
translations.idiomatic: Branch rivers and small channels should be deeply dredged during farming slack, using the excavated earth to raise the dikes.

sentences.zh: 」並敕部議行。

translations.literal: " All were ordered referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: All were referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.

sentences.zh: 又言：「道經宿州靈壁，見溝洫不通，積雨成潦，請飭安徽巡撫疏濬。

translations.literal: He also said: "Passing through Su Prefecture and Lingbi, I saw drains blocked and accumulated rain forming floods; I request that the Anhui governor be ordered to dredge and clear them.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Passing through Su Prefecture and Lingbi, I saw blocked drains and rains pooling into floods; I ask that the Anhui governor be ordered to dredge them.

sentences.zh: 」上嘉毓珣實陳。

translations.literal: The emperor praised Yuxun's candid reporting.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised Yuxun for reporting candidly.

sentences.zh: 五年，還廣東，巡撫楊文乾劾署巡撫阿克敦、布政使官達，上命通政使留保等往按。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, returning to Guangdong, Governor Yang Wenqian impeached acting Governor Akedun and Provincial Treasurer Guan Da; the emperor ordered Privy Council Secretary Liu Bao and others to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, on returning to Guangdong, Governor Yang Wenqian impeached acting Governor Akedun and Provincial Treasurer Guan Da; the emperor dispatched Privy Council Secretary Liu Bao and others to investigate.

sentences.zh: 毓珣失察，當下吏議，上命寬之。

translations.literal: Yuxun was held accountable for failure to detect the wrongdoing and should have been referred to officials for deliberation; the emperor ordered leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Yuxun was liable for failure to detect the wrongdoing and should have faced disciplinary proceedings; the emperor ordered leniency.

sentences.zh: 尋調江南河道總督。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to director-general of river works in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was transferred to director-general of Jiangnan river works.

sentences.zh: 上以天然壩洩水，慮溢浸民田，命毓珣相度築堤束水歸湖。

translations.literal: Because the Tianran Dam discharged water, the emperor feared overflow would inundate farmland and ordered Yuxun to survey and build dikes to constrain the water and return it to the lake.
translations.idiomatic: Concerned that the Tianran Dam's discharge would flood farmland, the emperor ordered Yuxun to survey the site and build dikes to channel the water back into the lake.

sentences.zh: 毓珣疏言：「天然南、北二壩分洩水勢，年年開放，堤口殘缺。

translations.literal: Yuxun memorialized: "The Tianran south and north dams divide and discharge the water's force; they are opened every year and the embankment mouths are worn and broken.
translations.idiomatic: Yuxun reported: "The Tianran south and north dams divide and release water pressure; they are opened yearly, and the embankment mouths are worn and breached.

sentences.zh: 當如上指築堤束水，請於南岸王家庵至趙家莊築新堤一道。

translations.literal: As the emperor directed, dikes should be built to constrain the water; I request building a new dike from Wangjia'an to Zhaojiazhuang on the south bank.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor directed, dikes should be built to channel the water; I propose a new dike from Wangjia'an to Zhaojiazhuang on the south bank.

sentences.zh: 舊堤尾距湖尚二十餘裡，請於南岸馬家圩至應家集、北岸周家圩至李艮橋，各築新堤一道，並將南北舊堤加培高廣，庶兩堤夾束湍流，無患旁溢。

translations.literal: The old dike end is still more than twenty li from the lake; I request new dikes from Majiawei to Yingjiaji on the south bank and from Zhoujiawei to Ligeng Bridge on the north bank, and that the old north and south dikes be raised and widened, so that the two dikes will constrain the turbulent flow and there will be no fear of side overflow.
translations.idiomatic: The old dike still ends more than twenty li from the lake; I propose new dikes from Majiawei to Yingjiaji on the south bank and from Zhoujiawei to Ligeng Bridge on the north bank, plus raising and widening the old north and south dikes, so the pair will channel the turbulent flow and prevent spillover.

sentences.zh: 」上又以高家堰為蓄清敵黃關鍵，發帑百萬，命毓珣籌畫。

translations.literal: The emperor also regarded the Gaojia Weir as the key to storing clear water against the Yellow River and allocated a million taels from the treasury, ordering Yuxun to plan the works.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also saw the Gaojia Weir as crucial for storing clear water against the Yellow River, allocated a million taels, and ordered Yuxun to plan the project.

sentences.zh: 毓珣疏言：「高家堰石堤，自武家墩至黃莊，地高工固，惟侯二門等四壩，及小黃莊至山盱古溝東壩，當一律加高。

translations.literal: Yuxun memorialized: "The stone dike at Gaojia Weir, from Wujiadun to Huangzhuang, is on high ground and solidly built; only the four sluices including Hou'ermen and the eastern sluice from Xiaohuangzhuang to the ancient trench at Shanxu need uniform raising.
translations.idiomatic: Yuxun reported: "The stone dike at Gaojia Weir from Wujiadun to Huangzhuang sits on high ground and is solid; only the four sluices including Hou'ermen and the eastern sluice from Xiaohuangzhuang to the ancient trench at Shanxu need uniform raising.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「各堤加培高廣，宜視地勢緩急、舊堤厚薄，分年修增，期三年而畢。

translations.literal: " He also said: "In raising and widening the various dikes, urgency should depend on terrain and old dike thickness; repairs should be phased over years, to be completed in three years.
translations.idiomatic: "He also said: "Raising and widening the various dikes should depend on terrain urgency and old dike thickness, with phased repairs over three years.

sentences.zh: 嗣後仍按年以次加培。

translations.literal: Thereafter annual additions should continue in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward annual strengthening should continue in sequence.

sentences.zh: 」又請修築宿遷鈔關前、桃源沈家莊河堤，瓜洲由閘上游濬越河一道，並建草壩束水。

translations.literal: He also requested repairing the river dike before the Suqian toll station and at Shenjiazhuang in Taoyuan, dredging a bypass channel upstream of the Guazhou sluice, and building grass weirs to constrain the water.
translations.idiomatic: He also requested repairs to the river dike before the Suqian toll station and at Shenjiazhuang in Taoyuan, dredging a bypass channel upstream of the Guazhou sluice, and building grass weirs to channel the water.

sentences.zh: 諸疏入，並報可。

translations.literal: When the memorials were submitted, all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: All the memorials were approved.

sentences.zh: 毓珣積瘁遘疾，上賜以藥餌，命其子刑部郎中傳熹偕御醫馳驛往視。

translations.literal: Yuxun, worn down by accumulated labor, fell ill; the emperor bestowed medicine and ordered his son, Penalty Department Director Fu Xi, to accompany an imperial physician post-haste to attend him.
translations.idiomatic: Worn down by years of labor, Yuxun fell ill; the emperor sent medicine and ordered his son Fu Xi, a director in the Ministry of Punishments, to accompany an imperial physician post-haste to his bedside.

sentences.zh: 未至，毓珣卒，賜祭葬，諡溫僖。

translations.literal: Before they arrived, Yuxun died and was granted funeral sacrifices and burial honors, with the posthumous title Wenxi.
translations.idiomatic: Before they arrived Yuxun died; he was granted funeral rites and burial honors with the posthumous title Wenxi.

sentences.zh: 裴幰度，字晉武，山西曲沃人。

translations.literal: Pei Xiandu, styled Jinwu, was a native of Quwo in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xiandu, styled Jinwu, was a native of Quwo in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 少為諸生，工詩，能書畫。

translations.literal: In youth he was a student, skilled at poetry and adept at calligraphy and painting.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was a student, skilled in poetry and adept at calligraphy and painting.

sentences.zh: 入貲為主事。

translations.literal: He purchased office and became a director.
translations.idiomatic: He purchased office and became a director.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十五年，授刑部主事。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year of Kangxi, he was appointed a director in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 35 he was appointed a director in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 洊擢戶部郎中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He rose repeatedly to director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，授雲南澂江知府，調廣南。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year, he was appointed prefect of Chengjiang in Yunnan and was transferred to Guangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-ninth year he was appointed prefect of Chengjiang in Yunnan and transferred to Guangnan.

sentences.zh: 以大計入覲，聖祖聞其能詩，命題應制，稱旨。

translations.literal: At the triennial assessment he came to audience; the Kangxi Emperor, having heard of his poetry, set a topic for an impromptu composition, which pleased him.
translations.idiomatic: At the triennial assessment he came to court; the Kangxi Emperor, hearing of his poetry, set a topic for an impromptu poem, which pleased him.

sentences.zh: 五十五年，遷河東鹽運使，尋改兩浙。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year, he was transferred to salt transport commissioner of Hedong, and soon afterward to the Two Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fifth year he was transferred to salt transport commissioner of Hedong, then soon to the Two Zhe.

sentences.zh: 海寧築塘，巡撫徐元度檄幰度董其事。

translations.literal: When sea dikes were built at Haining, Governor Xu Yuandu ordered Xiandu to supervise the project.
translations.idiomatic: When sea dikes were being built at Haining, Governor Xu Yuandu ordered Xiandu to supervise the work.

sentences.zh: 潮大至，撼塘，塘欲裂，幰度據地坐督役力護，久之乃定。

translations.literal: The tide surged, shaking the dike, which was near rupture; Xiandu sat on the ground to direct the workers and forcefully protect it, and after a long time it stabilized.
translations.idiomatic: A great tide shook the dike until it nearly broke; Xiandu sat on the ground directing the laborers and held the line until, after a long time, it held.

sentences.zh: 幰度自是中濕，病重膇，終其身。

translations.literal: From then on he remained damp at the middle, severely afflicted with edema for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he suffered chronic dampness at the waist, severe edema afflicting him for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，遷湖北按察使。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year, he was transferred to provincial surveillance commissioner of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-ninth year he was transferred to provincial surveillance commissioner of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 六十年，遷貴州布政使。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year, he was transferred to provincial administration commissioner of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year he became provincial administration commissioner of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，擢江西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng, he was promoted to governor of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1 he was promoted to governor of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 九江舊設關榷稅，後徙湖口。

translations.literal: Jiujiang formerly had a customs station for collecting taxes; it was later moved to Hukou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiujiang once had a customs station for tax collection; it was later moved to Hukou.

sentences.zh: 湖口當江、湖衝，水急，商舟時覆溺。

translations.literal: Hukou stands at the confluence of river and lake; the water is swift and merchant vessels often capsize and drown.
translations.idiomatic: Hukou lies where river and lake meet; the current is fierce and merchant vessels often capsize.

sentences.zh: 幰度疏言：「九江舊關，上有龍開河、官牌夾，下有老鶴塘、白水港，地勢寬平，泊舟安穩。

translations.literal: Xiandu memorialized: "The old Jiujiang customs station had Longkai River and Guanpai Gorge upstream and Old Crane Pond and Baishui Harbor downstream; the terrain is broad and level and mooring is secure.
translations.idiomatic: Xiandu reported: "The old Jiujiang customs station lay upstream of Longkai River and Guanpai Gorge and downstream of Old Crane Pond and Baishui Harbor, where the terrain is broad and mooring is safe.

sentences.zh: 離湖四十里曰大姑塘，為商舟所必經，水漲則有女兒港、張家套，皆可泊舟；

translations.literal: Forty li from the lake is Dagutang, which merchant vessels must pass; when water is high, Nü'er Harbor and Zhangjia Bay can both moor vessels;
translations.idiomatic: Forty li from the lake lies Dagutang, which all merchant vessels must pass; when water is high, Nü'er Harbor and Zhangjia Bay both offer moorings;

sentences.zh: 水落則平湖一線，夾岸泥沙，無風濤礁石之險。

translations.literal: when water is low, there is only a narrow strip of flat lake; the banks are sand and mud, without the danger of wind, waves, or reefs.
translations.idiomatic: when water is low only a narrow flat channel remains, with sand and mud banks but none of the hazards of wind, waves, or reefs.

sentences.zh: 請仍移關九江，而於大姑塘設口分抽。

translations.literal: I request that the customs station be moved back to Jiujiang, and that a branch collection point be set up at Dagutang for fractional levy.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the customs station be restored to Jiujiang and a branch collection point established at Dagutang.

sentences.zh: 」上令會同總督查弼納料理。

translations.literal: " The Emperor ordered that it be handled jointly with Governor-General Zhabina.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Governor-General Zhabina to take charge of the matter jointly.

sentences.zh: 南昌、袁州、瑞州三府賦額，明沿陳友諒之舊，視他府偏重。

translations.literal: The tax quotas of the three prefectures Nanchang, Yuanzhou, and Ruizhou, in the Ming following Chen Youliang's old amounts, were heavier than those of other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The tax quotas for Nanchang, Yuanzhou, and Ruizhou had been set in the Ming along Chen Youliang's old schedule and weighed more heavily than those of other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 順治間、減袁、瑞二府賦額，而南昌未及。

translations.literal: During Shunzhi the quotas of Yuan and Rui were reduced, but Nanchang had not yet been addressed.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shunzhi the quotas for Yuanzhou and Ruizhou were cut, but Nanchang's had not yet been adjusted.

sentences.zh: 幰度疏言：「常賦未易屢更，同省實難歧視。

translations.literal: Xiandu memorialized: "Regular land tax is not easily changed repeatedly; within one province it is hard to apply unequal treatment.
translations.idiomatic: Xiandu reported: "Regular land tax cannot be revised again and again, and within a single province it is hard to treat counties differently.

sentences.zh: 請將南昌賦額視袁、瑞二府同予核減。

translations.literal: I request that Nanchang's quota be reviewed and reduced on the same basis as the two prefectures Yuan and Rui.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that Nanchang's quota be audited and reduced to match Yuanzhou and Ruizhou.

sentences.zh: 」下部議減南昌浮額七萬五千五百兩有奇。

translations.literal: " The ministry deliberated and agreed to reduce Nanchang's inflated quota by more than seventy-five thousand five hundred taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry approved a reduction of Nanchang's excess quota by more than 75,500 taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 福建、廣東流民入江西，就山結棚以居，蓺靛葉、煙草，謂之「棚民」，往往出為盜。

translations.literal: Migrants from Fujian and Guangdong entered Jiangxi, built shed settlements on the mountains to live, cultivated indigo leaves and tobacco, and were called "shed people"; they often turned to banditry.
translations.idiomatic: Migrants from Fujian and Guangdong settled in Jiangxi's hills in shed villages, growing indigo and tobacco. Known as "shed folk," many turned to banditry.

sentences.zh: 萬載溫上貴、寧州劉允公等，皆以棚民為亂，幰度捕治論如律。

translations.literal: Wen Shanggui of Wanzai, Liu Yungong of Ningzhou, and others all raised rebellions with shed people; Xiandu captured and punished them according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Shanggui of Wanzai and Liu Yungong of Ningzhou led shed-folk rebellions; Xiandu captured them and punished them by law.

sentences.zh: 上令編保甲，幰度疏言：「棚民良莠淆雜，去留無定，或散居山箐，或為土民傭工墾地。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the organization of baojia; Xiandu memorialized: "Shed people mingle good and bad; they come and go without fixed residence, some scattered in mountain ravines, some hired by local people to reclaim land.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered baojia registration; Xiandu reported: "Shed folk mixed the law-abiding with the unruly, moving without fixed abode—some scattered in mountain ravines, others hired out to local farmers to clear land.

sentences.zh: 臣飭屬嚴察，凡萬五千餘戶，編甲造冊，按年入籍。

translations.literal: Your subject has ordered subordinates to investigate strictly; in all more than fifteen thousand households have been registered in baojia, books made, and enrolled year by year.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered strict inspections; more than 15,000 households were registered in baojia rolls and enrolled annually.

sentences.zh: 」上獎勉之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor praised and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor commended and encouraged him.

sentences.zh: 上聞江西里長催徵累民，民多尚邪教，諭幰度禁革。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard that Jiangxi village heads' tax collection oppressed the people and that the people widely followed heterodox cults; he instructed Xiandu to prohibit and reform this.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Jiangxi village heads' tax collection was oppressing the people and that heterodox cults had wide following, the Emperor instructed Xiandu to ban and reform the practice.

sentences.zh: 幰度疏言：「臣察知里長累民，已勒石永禁，令糧戶自封投櫃。

translations.literal: Xiandu memorialized: "Your subject has found that village heads oppress the people; I have had a stele carved to forbid this permanently and ordered grain households to seal and submit payment themselves at the chest.
translations.idiomatic: Xiandu reported: "I found village heads were burdening the people, had a stele carved to forbid it permanently, and ordered grain households to seal and pay their taxes directly at the collection chest.

sentences.zh: 距城較遠畸零小戶，原輪僱交納者聽其便，仍嚴防不得乾累。

translations.literal: For scattered small households far from cities who originally took turns hiring others to pay, they may continue as convenient, but strict guard must be kept against improper impositions.
translations.idiomatic: Scattered small households far from town who had paid by rotation might continue as before, but officials were strictly forbidden to impose extra burdens on them.

sentences.zh: 邪教自當捕治，醫卜星相往往假其術以惑民，雖非邪教，亦當以時嚴懲。

translations.literal: Heterodox cults should of course be arrested and punished; medicine, divination, and physiognomy often use their arts to mislead the people; though not heterodox cults, they should also be severely punished in season.
translations.idiomatic: Heterodox cults should be arrested and punished; physicians, diviners, and astrologers often used their arts to mislead the people, and though not cults themselves, they too should be punished when the occasion warranted.

sentences.zh: 」上深嘉之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor deeply commended him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor warmly commended him.

sentences.zh: 總督查弼納議開廣信封禁山，諭幰度酌度。

translations.literal: Governor-General Zhabina proposed opening Guangfeng's sealed-forbidden mountain; the Emperor instructed Xiandu to consider and decide.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Zhabina proposed opening Guangfeng's Fengjin Mountain; the Emperor told Xiandu to weigh the matter and decide.

sentences.zh: 幰度疏言：「封禁山舊名銅塘山，相傳產銅，然有名無實，故自明封禁至今。

translations.literal: Xiandu memorialized: "Fengjin Mountain was formerly called Tongtang Mountain; tradition says it produced copper, but the name did not match reality, hence it has been sealed and forbidden since the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Xiandu reported: "Fengjin Mountain was once called Tongtang Mountain; legend held it produced copper, but the name had no basis in fact, and it had been closed since the Ming.

sentences.zh: 順治間有議採木者，郡縣力陳不便，勒碑永禁。

translations.literal: During Shunzhi there were proposals to harvest timber; the prefecture and counties strongly stated the inconvenience and had a stele carved to forbid it permanently.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shunzhi timber harvesting had been proposed; prefecture and county officials argued strongly against it and had a stele carved to forbid it forever.

sentences.zh: 臣揆查弼納意，或以棚民巢穴在此山中，故為破巢搗穴之計。

translations.literal: Your subject surmises Governor-General Zhabina's intent: perhaps because shed people's nests are in this mountain, hence a plan to destroy nest and lair.
translations.idiomatic: He inferred that Zhabina's aim was to destroy the shed folk's hideouts in the hills—a plan to "break the nest and smash the den."

sentences.zh: 此山荊榛充塞，稔毒滋藏，並非有梗化頑民盤踞在內。

translations.literal: This mountain is choked with thorns and brambles where poisons fester; there are not obstinate unreformed people occupying it within.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain was choked with thorn and bramble where mischief festered; no stubborn, unreformed people were actually encamped inside.

sentences.zh: 臣詳度此山開則擾累，封則安寧，成案俱存，確有可據。

translations.literal: Your subject has fully considered: opening this mountain brings disturbance and burden; sealing brings peace; decided cases all exist and are indeed supportable.
translations.idiomatic: He concluded that opening the mountain would bring trouble while keeping it closed preserved peace; precedents on both sides were on record and well founded.

sentences.zh: 」諭曰：「當開則不得因循，當禁則不宜依違。

translations.literal: " An edict said: "When it should be opened, one must not procrastinate; when it should be forbidden, one must not vacillate.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied: "When something should be opened, do not delay; when it should be forbidden, do not waver.

sentences.zh: 但不存貪功之念，實心為地方興利除害，何事不可為？

translations.literal: But without harboring thoughts of greedy merit-seeking, if one sincerely promotes benefit and removes harm for the locality, what cannot be done?
translations.idiomatic: But put aside thoughts of grabbing credit; if you earnestly seek the region's good and remove its ills, what cannot be done?

sentences.zh: 在卿等秉公相度時宜而酌定之。

translations.literal: It rests with you to weigh the times impartially and decide accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: It is for you to weigh the circumstances impartially and settle the matter.

sentences.zh: 」仍封禁如初。

translations.literal: " It remained sealed and forbidden as before.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain remained closed as before.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷戶部侍郎，擢​​左都御史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was transferred to vice minister of Revenue and promoted to left censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he became vice minister of Revenue and was promoted to left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 上遣侍郎邁柱勘江西諸州縣倉穀，命幰度留任。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Vice Minister Maizhu to inspect granary grain in Jiangxi's prefectures and counties, and ordered Xiandu to remain at his post.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Vice Minister Maizhu to audit granary grain in Jiangxi's prefectures and counties and ordered Xiandu to stay in office.

sentences.zh: 邁柱疏言：「倉穀虧空甚多，例定穀一石折銀二錢，州縣交代，按此數接收，不敷糴補。

translations.literal: Maizhu memorialized: "Granary grain is greatly deficient; by regulation one shi of grain converts to two mace of silver; at prefectural and county handovers this rate is used for receipt, and shortfalls are bought to replenish.
translations.idiomatic: Maizhu reported: "Granary stocks were badly depleted; by regulation one shi of grain was reckoned at two mace of silver, and at handover prefectures and counties were to receive grain at that rate and buy grain to make up shortfalls.

sentences.zh: 」上奪幰度及歷任布政使張楷、陳安策官，命以所存摺價買穀還倉。

translations.literal: " The Emperor stripped Xiandu and successive provincial commissioners Zhang Kai and Chen Ance of their ranks and ordered them to use saved salary to buy grain and restore the granaries.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor stripped Xiandu and former provincial commissioners Zhang Kai and Chen Ance of rank and ordered them to use their saved salary to buy grain and refill the granaries.

sentences.zh: 十年，事畢，釋還裡。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, when the matter was finished, he was released to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, when the matter was settled, he was released and sent home.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qianlong, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Qianlong 5.

sentences.zh: 子宗錫，入貲為同知。

translations.literal: His son Zong Xi purchased office as an assistant prefect.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zong Xi bought office and became an assistant prefect.

sentences.zh: 十五年，授山東濟南同知，屢遷轉。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he was appointed assistant prefect of Jinan in Shandong and was repeatedly transferred.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was appointed assistant prefect of Jinan in Shandong and moved through several posts.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，授直隸霸昌道，遷直隸按察使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, he was appointed Baxing Circuit intendant of Zhili and was transferred to provincial surveillance commissioner of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he was appointed Baxing Circuit intendant of Zhili and then provincial surveillance commissioner of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「古北口外山場產菠蘿樹，此即橡樹，葉可飼蠶。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Beyond Gubeikou the mountain lands produce boluo trees; these are oak trees whose leaves can feed silkworms.
translations.idiomatic: He reported: "Beyond Gubeikou the hills grow boluo trees—that is, oaks whose leaves can feed silkworms.

sentences.zh: 臣在濟東，飭屬通栽，頗有成效。

translations.literal: When your subject was in eastern Ji, I ordered subordinates to plant them widely, with considerable success.
translations.idiomatic: When I served in eastern Shandong I ordered widespread planting with considerable success.

sentences.zh: 請令用東省養蠶法，廣栽試養。

translations.literal: I request orders to use Shandong's silkworm-rearing method, plant widely, and trial rear.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that Shandong's silkworm-rearing methods be applied, with wide planting and trial cultivation.

sentences.zh: 」命交總督方觀承試行。

translations.literal: " He was ordered to hand the matter to Governor-General Fang Guancheng for trial implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Governor-General Fang Guancheng to try the scheme.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，以母憂去官。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year, he left office on account of his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year he left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 宗錫在任，誤應驛站車馬，部議當降調。

translations.literal: While Zong Xi was in office, he mistakenly supplied post station horses and vehicles; the ministry deliberated that he should be demoted and transferred.
translations.idiomatic: While still in office Zong Xi had mistakenly furnished post horses and carts; the ministry recommended demotion and transfer.

sentences.zh: 總督楊廷璋諮部，言宗錫當自行檢舉。

translations.literal: Governor-General Yang Tingzhang consulted the ministry, saying Zong Xi ought to have reported himself.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Yang Tingzhang consulted the ministry, arguing that Zong Xi should have reported himself.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「宗錫，朕知其為人，頗可造就。

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed: "Zong Xi — I know his character; he is quite capable of cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "I know Zong Xi's character; he shows real promise.

sentences.zh: 按察使管理驛站，偶有一二誤應，原屬公過。

translations.literal: A surveillance commissioner manages post stations; an occasional mistaken supply is originally a public lapse.
translations.idiomatic: A surveillance commissioner oversees post stations; an occasional mistake in furnishing horses is an ordinary official lapse.

sentences.zh: 今已丁憂，安得自行檢舉？

translations.literal: Now he is in mourning; how can he report himself?
translations.idiomatic: He is in mourning now—how can he report himself?

sentences.zh: 廷璋乃令作此趨避，愛之適以害之也。

translations.literal: Tingzhang thus had him make this evasive move — loving him only to harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhang's evasive maneuver only harmed the man he meant to protect.

sentences.zh: 」三十五年，宗錫服將闋，仍授直隸按察使。

translations.literal: " In the thirty-fifth year, as Zong Xi's mourning period was about to end, he was again appointed provincial surveillance commissioner of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year, as his mourning was nearing its end, Zong Xi was again appointed provincial surveillance commissioner of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 俄擢安徽布政使，就遷巡撫。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to provincial administration commissioner of Anhui and immediately transferred to governor.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to provincial administration commissioner of Anhui and immediately made governor.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「安慶瀕江舊有漳葭港，上通潛山、太湖、望江三縣，下達江，漕艘商舶往來停泊，淤久漸成平陸。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Anqing borders the river and once had Zhangjia Harbor, linking upstream to the three counties Qianshan, Taihu, and Wangjiang and downstream to the river; grain transport and merchant vessels moored there, but after long siltation it gradually became flat land.
translations.idiomatic: He reported: "Anqing once had Zhangjia Harbor on the river, linking upstream to Qianshan, Taihu, and Wangjiang and downstream to the Yangtze, where grain boats and merchant ships had moored until long siltation turned it to dry land.

sentences.zh: 前巡撫張楷於上游別開新河，地高水急，重載逆上，遇風每虞覆溺。

translations.literal: The former governor Zhang Kai opened a new canal upstream; the ground is high and water swift; heavy loads going upstream, they often feared capsizing when wind struck.
translations.idiomatic: Former governor Zhang Kai had cut a new canal upstream, but the ground was high and the current fierce; heavily laden boats going upstream often risked capsizing in wind.

sentences.zh: 請仍濬漳葭港故道。

translations.literal: I request restoring dredging of Zhangjia Harbor's old channel.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that Zhangjia Harbor's old channel be dredged again.

sentences.zh: 」命總督高晉履勘，如宗錫議行。

translations.literal: " The Emperor ordered Governor-General Gao Jin to inspect on site and implement as Zong Xi proposed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Governor-General Gao Jin to inspect on site and carry out Zong Xi's plan.

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「鳳、泗所屬州縣，高地宜多作池塘，低地宜厚築圩圍，以備灌溉、資捍禦。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "In the prefectures and counties under Feng and Si, high ground should have more ponds dug, low ground should have thicker dikes and embankments built, to prepare irrigation and aid defense.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged that in the Fengyang and Sizhou region high ground should get more ponds and low ground stronger dikes and embankments, for irrigation and flood defense.

sentences.zh: 鳳陽地多高岡曠野，不宜五穀，令視土宜種樹。

translations.literal: Fengyang's land has many high hills and open wastes, unsuitable for the five grains; order planting trees according to soil suitability.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyang's high hills and open wastes were poor for grain; he ordered trees planted wherever the soil suited them.

sentences.zh: 」諭獎其留心本務。

translations.literal: " An edict praised his attention to fundamental duties.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised his attention to the fundamentals of governance.

sentences.zh: 四十年，調雲南。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year, he was transferred to Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year he was transferred to Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 旋命署貴州。

translations.literal: He was soon ordered to serve as acting governor of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to serve as acting governor of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「貴州地處邊圉，請敕部撥銀三十萬貯司庫。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Guizhou lies on the frontier; I request imperial orders to the ministry to allocate three hundred thousand taels of silver for storage in the provincial treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the ministry allocate 300,000 taels of silver to the provincial treasury, citing Guizhou's frontier position.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 又疏請增設鎮遠稅口，上嚴斥不許。

translations.literal: He also memorialized requesting an added tax station at Zhenyuan; the Emperor sternly rebuked him and refused.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to add a tax station at Zhenyuan; the Emperor sharply refused.

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「貴州額輸京師及湖廣白鉛歲七百餘萬斤，鉛廠僅三處，年久產絀。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Guizhou's quota delivery to the capital and to Huguang of white lead is more than seven million jin per year; there are only three lead works, long worked and yielding short.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported that Guizhou owed more than seven million jin of white lead yearly to the capital and Huguang, but only three lead works remained and long operation had depleted their output.

sentences.zh: 臣察知松桃廳巴壩山、遵義縣新砦產鉛，近水次，已飭設廠，歲各得鉛百餘萬斤。

translations.literal: Your subject has found that Baba Mountain in Songtao Department and Xinzai in Zunyi County produce lead, near waterways; works have been ordered established, each yielding more than a million jin of lead per year.
translations.idiomatic: He had found lead at Baba Mountain in Songtao and Xinzai in Zunyi, both near waterways; new works there each yielded more than a million jin a year.

sentences.zh: 分撥京師、湖廣，歲節省運費銀四萬三千有奇。

translations.literal: Allocated to the capital and Huguang, this saves more than forty-three thousand taels of transport costs per year.
translations.idiomatic: Supplying the capital and Huguang from these sites saved more than 43,000 taels in transport costs each year.

sentences.zh: 」得旨嘉允。

translations.literal: " The imperial reply commended and approved.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved and commended the plan.

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「貴州古州有牛皮大箐，亙數百里，列屯置軍，應將箐內平曠之土開墾成田，寓防於屯，安屯養軍。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "In Guizhou's Guzhou is Niupi Great Ravine, spanning several hundred li; garrisons and troops are deployed in rows; the flat open land within the ravine should be opened and reclaimed as fields, combining defense with colonies, settling colonies to support troops.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed that in Guzhou's Niupi Great Ravine, which ran for hundreds of li and was lined with military colonies, the level land inside should be opened to fields so colonies could both garrison and feed the troops.

sentences.zh: 丹江雷公院地平衍，可墾四五百畝，歐收、甬荒高箐二地畸零，可墾三四百畝，應令附近震威堡屯軍派撥試墾，並於丹江營移撥千總一、兵五十，入箐設卡駐守。

translations.literal: The level ground at Leigongyuan in Danjiang can be reclaimed as four or five hundred mu; Oushou and Yonghuang Gaojing are scattered plots where three or four hundred mu can be reclaimed; troops from nearby Zhenweibao colony should be assigned for trial reclamation, and from Danjiang garrison one company commander and fifty soldiers should be moved in to set up checkpoints and garrison the ravine.
translations.idiomatic: At Leigongyuan in Danjiang four or five hundred mu of level ground could be cleared; scattered plots at Oushou and Yonghuang Gaojing could yield three or four hundred mu more. He proposed assigning nearby Zhenweibao colonists to trial cultivation and moving one company commander and fifty soldiers from the Danjiang garrison into the ravine to man checkpoints.

sentences.zh: 」時上已命宗錫還雲南，命交後政圖思德如所議行。

translations.literal: " At this time the Emperor had already ordered Zong Xi back to Yunnan; he ordered his successor Tusi De to implement as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Emperor had already recalled Zong Xi to Yunnan and ordered his successor Tusi De to carry out the plan.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，以病乞解任。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year, he begged to resign on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year he asked to resign because of illness.

sentences.zh: 旋卒，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: He soon died and was granted funeral rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after and was granted state funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 唐執玉，字益功，江南武進人。

translations.literal: Tang Zhiyu, styled Yigong, was a native of Wujin in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Zhiyu, styled Yigong, was a native of Wujin in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十二年進士，授浙江德清知縣。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the forty-second year of Kangxi, he was appointed magistrate of Deqing in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Kangxi 42, he was appointed magistrate of Deqing in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 德清盛科第，多鉅室，執玉執法無所撓。

translations.literal: Deqing abounded in degree holders and great households; Zhiyu enforced the law without bending.
translations.idiomatic: Deqing produced many degree holders and wealthy families, yet Zhiyu enforced the law without yielding.

sentences.zh: 將編審，吏以例餽金，執玉卻之，而罪其吏。

translations.literal: When a cadastral review was impending, a clerk offered gold by custom; Zhiyu refused it and punished the clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Before a cadastral review a clerk offered the customary bribe; Zhiyu refused it and punished the man.

sentences.zh: 召縣民親勘，有田無糧者令自首，有糧無田者除之，富無隱糧，貧無賠累。

translations.literal: He summoned county people for personal survey: those with land but no tax were ordered to confess; those with tax but no land had it removed; the rich had no hidden tax, the poor no forced liability.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the people to survey the land in person: holders of untaxed land were told to confess, tax entries without land were struck off, the rich could not hide grain dues, and the poor were spared wrongful burdens.

sentences.zh: 行取工部主事，考選戶科給事中。

translations.literal: Selected directly as a director in the Ministry of Works, he was chosen by examination as a supervising censor in the Revenue Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Selected for the Ministry of Works as a director, he was then chosen by examination as a supervising censor in the Revenue Bureau.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，疏言：「戶部錢糧款項最易作弊，當先驅除作弊之人。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year, he memorialized: "The Ministry of Revenue's money and grain items are easiest to tamper with; one must first drive out those who tamper.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-eighth year he reported: "Revenue accounts are easiest to falsify; the first step is to remove those who falsify them.

sentences.zh: 乃有所謂'缺主'者，或一人佔一司，或數人共一省，佔為世業，句通內外書吏，舞文弄法，當嚴行查禁。

translations.literal: There are so-called 'post masters' who occupy one bureau alone or several share a province, making it hereditary trade, colluding with inside and outside clerks, twisting documents and manipulating law — this must be strictly investigated and forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: So-called 'post masters' monopolized whole bureaus or whole provinces as hereditary trades, colluding with clerks inside and out to twist documents and bend the law; this had to be rigorously suppressed.

sentences.zh: 」因劾山西司缺主沈天生包攬捐馬事例，下九卿議，逮治。

translations.literal: " He therefore impeached Shen Tiansheng, post master of the Shanxi bureau, for monopolizing the donated-horse precedent; the case went to the Nine Ministers for deliberation and he was arrested for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Shen Tiansheng, post master of the Shanxi bureau, for monopolizing the donated-horse quota; the case went to the Nine Ministers and Shen was arrested.

sentences.zh: 六十年，遷鴻臚寺卿。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year, he was transferred to chief minister of the Court of State Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year he became chief minister of the Court of State Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 歷奉天府府丞、大理寺少卿。

translations.literal: He served successively as vice prefect of Fengtian Prefecture and vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as vice prefect of Fengtian Prefecture and vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年，歲三遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongzheng, within one year he was thrice promoted to vice minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 2 he was promoted three times within a single year to vice minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 五年，擢左都御史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was promoted to left censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was promoted to left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 七年，命署直隸總督。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he was ordered to serve as acting governor-general of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was ordered to serve as acting governor-general of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 執玉治事勤，州縣稍歉收，必籌畫賑恤。

translations.literal: Zhiyu was diligent in governance; whenever a prefecture or county had even slight crop shortfall, he always planned relief.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyu was a tireless administrator; whenever any prefecture or county reported even a modest harvest shortfall, he organized relief.

sentences.zh: 隆平報產瑞禾三十三本，執玉於報秋成摺附奏，上嘉之。

translations.literal: Longping reported thirty-three stalks of auspicious grain; Zhiyu appended the report to his autumn harvest memorial and the Emperor commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Longping reported thirty-three stalks of auspicious grain; Zhiyu attached the report to his autumn harvest memorial and the Emperor commended him.

sentences.zh: 適貢荔支至，命以賜執玉，方有疾，治事如常。

translations.literal: Just then tribute lychees arrived; the Emperor ordered them given to Zhiyu, who though ill carried on governing as usual.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute lychees had just arrived; the Emperor ordered them sent to Zhiyu, who though ill continued governing as usual.

sentences.zh: 時宗人府府丞冀棟以醫進，上命視執玉疾，賜人葠，諭令：「愛養精神，量力治事。

translations.literal: At that time Ji Dong of the Imperial Clan Court entered as physician; the Emperor ordered him to treat Zhiyu's illness, bestowed ginseng, and instructed: "Cherish your spirit, govern within your strength.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Dong of the Imperial Clan Court had entered as physician; the Emperor sent him to treat Zhiyu, bestowed ginseng, and told him: "Conserve your strength and govern only as much as you can bear.

sentences.zh: 若欲棟料量方藥，保定咫尺，可再命之來也。

translations.literal: If you wish Dong to prescribe medicines, Baoding is close at hand; he can be ordered to come again.
translations.idiomatic: If you want Dong to prescribe again, Baoding is close—he can be summoned back.

sentences.zh: 」熱河徵落地稅，司其事者議增歲額，並於榜什營等地設口徵稅。

translations.literal: " The Rehe land tax was being collected; those in charge proposed increasing the annual quota and setting up collection points at Bangshiying and other places.
translations.idiomatic: When Rehe land tax was being collected, officials proposed raising the annual quota and adding collection points at Bangshiying and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 下執玉議，執玉言：「商稅多寡，視歲收豐歉，故止能折中定額。

translations.literal: The matter was sent to Zhiyu for deliberation; Zhiyu said: "The amount of merchant tax depends on harvest abundance or scarcity; thus one can only fix a median quota.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was referred to Zhiyu, who said: "Merchant tax yields depend on harvests, so one can only set a balanced fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 榜什營距一百八十餘裡，已收落地稅，又抽進路鈔銀，恐商賈不前，正稅反缺，請如舊便。

translations.literal: Bangshiying is more than one hundred eighty li distant; land tax has already been collected, and to levy transit-route silver again would fear merchants not coming forward and the regular tax falling short; I request keeping the old arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: Bangshiying lay more than 180 li away; land tax had already been collected there, and an added transit levy would discourage merchants and reduce regular revenue. He asked that the old arrangement stand.

sentences.zh: 」議乃寢。

translations.literal: " The proposal was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 長蘆巡鹽御史鄭禪寶以商人虧帑，請增鹽價，上以詢執玉。

translations.literal: Changlu salt censor Zheng Chanbao, because merchants had depleted the treasury, requested raising the salt price; the Emperor consulted Zhiyu.
translations.idiomatic: Changlu salt censor Zheng Chanbao, citing merchant losses against the treasury, asked to raise the salt price; the Emperor consulted Zhiyu.

sentences.zh: 執玉言：「上於商民無歧視。

translations.literal: Zhiyu said: "Your Majesty shows no discrimination between merchants and common people.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyu said: "Your Majesty treats merchants and common people alike.

sentences.zh: 諸商不謹身節用，先公後私，乃至虧帑。

translations.literal: The merchants did not restrain themselves and economize, putting public before private, until the treasury was depleted.
translations.idiomatic: The merchants failed to restrain themselves and put public funds before private gain until the treasury was drained.

sentences.zh: 欲增鹽價厲民，臣以為非宜。

translations.literal: To raise the salt price and burden the people — your subject considers this inappropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Raising the salt price to burden the people would be wrong, in my view.

sentences.zh: 」亦罷不行。

translations.literal: " That too was abandoned and not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: That proposal too was rejected.

sentences.zh: 八年春，入覲。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year, he came to audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eighth year he came to court.

sentences.zh: 灤、盧龍、遷安、撫寧、昌黎、樂亭諸州縣米貯喜峰口倉，虧二千五百餘石，執玉請視通州中、西二倉例免追償。

translations.literal: In the prefectures and counties of Luan, Lulong, Qian'an, Funing, Changli, and Laoting, grain stored in the Xifengkou granary was short by more than 2,500 shi; Zhiyu requested exemption from recovery pursuit following the precedent of Tongzhou's middle and west granaries.
translations.idiomatic: In Luan, Lulong, Qian'an, Funing, Changli, and Laoting, grain stored at Xifengkou granary was short by more than 2,500 shi; Zhiyu asked that recovery be waived as it had been for Tongzhou's middle and west granaries.

sentences.zh: 部議不許，上特允之。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated and did not permit it; the emperor personally granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry opposed the request, but the emperor approved it himself.

sentences.zh: 密雲城臨白河，舊築土木堤壩盡圮，僅存石堤。

translations.literal: Miyun city stood by the Bai River; old earthen and wooden dikes and dams had all collapsed, and only the stone dike remained.
translations.idiomatic: Miyun city lay on the Bai River; its old earthen and timber dikes had all fallen into ruin, leaving only a stone embankment standing.

sentences.zh: 上游有積土斜出，激水使怒，俗謂之「土嘴」。

translations.literal: Upstream there was accumulated earth jutting obliquely, stirring the water to rage; the common people called it an "earth snout."
translations.idiomatic: Upstream, a mound of silt jutted into the channel and drove the current into a fury; locally it was called an "earth snout."

sentences.zh: 執玉疏請疏治，使水得暢流；

translations.literal: Zhiyu memorialized requesting dredging and repair so the water could flow freely;
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyu memorialized asking that the obstruction be cleared so the river could run freely again;

sentences.zh: 仍築土堤，務堅厚，用榆囤載石為基，使輔石堤護縣城。

translations.literal: He also had an earthen dike built, making it solid and thick, using elm trestles loaded with stones as a foundation, so as to assist the stone dike in protecting the county seat.
translations.idiomatic: He further proposed building a sturdy earthen levee on a foundation of stone-filled elm cribs to buttress the stone dike and shield the county seat.

sentences.zh: 上褒其妥協，命於夏月水漲前竟工。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his sound arrangement and ordered the work finished before the summer flood season.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended his prudent plan and ordered the work completed before the summer rise.

sentences.zh: 遷兵部尚書，仍署總督。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of War and still held the governorship in an acting capacity.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of War while continuing to serve as acting governor-general.

sentences.zh: 是歲秋，積雨，永定、滹沱諸水皆盛漲。

translations.literal: That autumn there was persistent rain, and the Yongding, Hutuo, and other rivers all rose greatly.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, prolonged rains sent the Yongding, Hutuo, and other rivers into full flood.

sentences.zh: 執玉疏報災，上命侍郎牧可登、副都統阿魯等分往治賑。

translations.literal: Zhiyu memorialized reporting the disaster; the emperor ordered Vice Minister Mu Kedeng, Vice Lieutenant General Aru, and others to go separately to administer relief.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyu reported the flooding, and the emperor dispatched Vice Minister Mu Kedeng, Vice Lieutenant General Aru, and others to oversee relief in the affected areas.

sentences.zh: 執玉奏言：「諸州縣被水，消長不一。

translations.literal: Zhiyu memorialized: "The prefectures and counties struck by water vary in ebb and flow.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyu wrote: "Among the counties affected by floodwaters, conditions differ widely.

sentences.zh: 有上諭所及，而水消未成災者；

translations.literal: There are those covered by imperial edict whose waters have receded without becoming a disaster;
translations.idiomatic: Some places named in the imperial edict have already seen the water subside without serious damage;

sentences.zh: 有上諭所未及，而水大成災，田廬被淹，急須拯卹者：請飭治賑諸臣勘實。

translations.literal: There are those not covered by imperial edict where the water has become a great disaster, fields and homes inundated, urgently needing relief: I request that the officials sent to administer relief be ordered to investigate on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Others not mentioned in the edict have suffered severe flooding, with fields and dwellings under water and relief urgently needed: I ask that the relief commissioners be instructed to verify conditions on the ground.

sentences.zh: 」上特允之。

translations.literal: " The emperor personally granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the request at once.

sentences.zh: 國初以民地予滿洲將士，謂之「圈地」。

translations.literal: At the founding of the dynasty, civilian lands were granted to Manchu officers and soldiers; this was called "land enclosure."
translations.idiomatic: In the dynasty's early years, Han-held land was allotted to Manchu banner officers and soldiers in what was known as "land enclosure."

sentences.zh: 民地既圈，以鄰近州縣地撥補，糧額從舊貫，於是有寄糧；

translations.literal: Once civilian lands were enclosed, adjacent prefectural and county lands were reallocated as compensation, tax quotas following old practice—thus there arose "attached grain tax";
translations.idiomatic: When land was enclosed, neighboring counties would supply replacement plots while grain quotas stayed tied to the original registrations, creating what were called "attached grain quotas."

sentences.zh: 佃租戶移新地，於是有寄莊。

translations.literal: Tenant households moved to new lands, and thus there arose "attached estates."
translations.idiomatic: Tenants relocated to new plots as well, giving rise to "attached estates."

sentences.zh: 歷年既久，百弊叢起。

translations.literal: Many years having passed, a hundred abuses sprang up together.
translations.idiomatic: Over the years, abuses multiplied without number.

sentences.zh: 上令執玉勘察，更除改正，並舉懷安、宣化、萬全、寶坻、豐潤、三河諸縣為例。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Zhiyu to inspect, rectify and correct, citing Huai'an, Xuanhua, Wanquan, Baodi, Fengrun, Sanhe, and other counties as examples.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor directed Zhiyu to investigate and reform the system, using Huai'an, Xuanhua, Wanquan, Baodi, Fengrun, Sanhe, and other counties as illustrative cases.

sentences.zh: 執玉奏言：「此外所在皆有，如晉州武丘村、孔目莊，趙州馬圈村糧有在讚皇者；

translations.literal: Zhiyu memorialized: "Beyond these, such cases exist everywhere, as at Jizhou's Wuqiu Village and Kongmu Estate, where grain tax from Mazquan Village in Zhaozhou is registered in Zanhuang;
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyu reported: "Cases of this sort are found throughout the province—for example, grain tax from Wuqiu Village and Kongmu Estate in Jizhou, and from Mazquan Village in Zhaozhou, is registered in Zanhuang;

sentences.zh: 蔚縣夾道溝、細賢莊糧有在宣化者；

translations.literal: In Yu County's Jiadougou and Xixian Estate the grain tax is registered in Xuanhua;
translations.idiomatic: In Yu County, taxes from Jiadougou and Xixian Estate are owed in Xuanhua;

sentences.zh: 宣化井頭莊糧有在西寧者：官苦追呼，民勞跋涉。

translations.literal: In Xuanhua's Jingtou Estate the grain tax is registered in Xining: officials suffer from the strain of collection, the people from the toil of long journeys.
translations.idiomatic: And grain from Jingtou Estate in Xuanhua is collected in Xining—officials struggle to enforce payment, while peasants exhaust themselves in travel.

sentences.zh: 凡地在此處，糧寄彼處，皆令從地所在，糧隨產轉，此收彼除，不使有交錯之病，亦無庸存代徵之名，經界各正，田賦悉清。

translations.literal: Wherever land lay here and grain tax was attached there, all were ordered to follow the land's location, with tax shifting with the property; what was collected here was removed there, so there would be no disorder of overlap, nor any need to retain the name of proxy collection—boundaries were each set right, and field taxes all cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever land lay in one place but tax remained registered elsewhere, he ordered taxes to follow the land; assessments would be added here and removed there, eliminating confusion and proxy collection, with boundaries and land dues set straight.

sentences.zh: 」直隸驛馬一，每歲雜支大率至十兩。

translations.literal: " For each relay-horse station horse in Zhili, miscellaneous expenses annually generally reached ten taels.
translations.idiomatic: Each relay horse in Zhili had been costing roughly ten taels a year in miscellaneous expenses.

sentences.zh: 執玉奏定馬一每歲雜支三兩六錢。

translations.literal: Zhiyu memorialized fixing miscellaneous expenses at three taels six qian per horse per year.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyu fixed annual overhead at three taels six qian per horse.

sentences.zh: 昌平、延慶、宣化諸驛事煩​​，撥僻地馬協濟，而牧養仍責原驛。

translations.literal: The relay stations of Changping, Yanqing, Xuanhua, and others being busy, horses from remote stations were assigned to assist, yet feeding and care remained charged to the original stations.
translations.idiomatic: Busy stations at Changping, Yanqing, and Xuanhua borrowed horses from quieter posts, yet the home stations still bore the cost of upkeep.

sentences.zh: 執玉奏請改隸受協州縣牧養。

translations.literal: Zhiyu memorialized requesting that responsibility for feeding and care be transferred to the receiving counties and stations that borrowed the horses.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyu asked that horses on loan be placed under the care of the counties that used them.

sentences.zh: 皆下部議行。

translations.literal: All were referred to the ministry for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: All these proposals were referred to the ministry for approval and enactment.

sentences.zh: 直隸耗羨歸公，自雍正三年始。

translations.literal: In Zhili, surplus fees from grain transport were turned over to the public treasury, beginning in Yongzheng 3.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yongzheng 3, surplus grain-shipping fees in Zhili had been remitted to the public treasury.

sentences.zh: 部議元、二年耗羨在三年補納者，州縣充公用，仍當追償。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated that surplus fees from years 1 and 2 paid up in year 3, which counties had used for public expenses, should still be recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry ruled that surpluses from the first two years, paid in during the third and already spent by local governments, must nevertheless be recovered.

sentences.zh: 霸、文安等七州縣民借倉穀，逋米二萬一千石、穀一萬六千石各有奇，部議責州縣追償。

translations.literal: In Ba, Wen'an, and six other prefectures and counties the people had borrowed granary grain, owing more than 21,000 shi of rice and more than 16,000 shi of grain; the ministry deliberated holding the counties responsible for recovery.
translations.idiomatic: In Ba, Wen'an, and five other counties, peasants who had borrowed state grain still owed more than 21,000 shi of rice and 16,000 shi of millet; the ministry ordered local officials to collect the debts.

sentences.zh: 執玉言：「元、二年耗羨在未著令歸公以前，前督臣許州縣充公用。

translations.literal: Zhiyu said: "Surpluses from years 1 and 2, before the order requiring remittance to the public treasury, the former governor-general had permitted counties to use for public expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyu argued: "Surpluses from the first two years were spent locally before the policy requiring remittance took effect; the previous governor-general had expressly allowed that use.

sentences.zh: 今欲追償，是為小費而失大言。

translations.literal: Now to seek recovery is to grasp at small expense and lose great credibility.
translations.idiomatic: To demand repayment now would be penny-wise and faithless.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「倉穀民欠歷年已久，人產胥絕。

translations.literal: " He also said: "The people's debts of granary grain extend over many years; persons and property are utterly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "These granary debts are decades old; the debtors and their estates are utterly ruined.

sentences.zh: 今欲追償，此數十年官州縣者無慮百數，悉逮其子孫而加以追比，於情可憫。

translations.literal: Now to seek recovery—in these decades there have been no fewer than a hundred officials who served these counties; to seize all their descendants and press for collection is pitiable in human terms.
translations.idiomatic: To pursue payment now would mean hounding the descendants of perhaps a hundred former magistrates—a cruelty that warrants compassion.

sentences.zh: 」上並如執玉議，寬之。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved all of Zhiyu's proposals and granted relief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted Zhiyu's recommendations and waived the debts.

sentences.zh: 九年，以病甚乞解任，許之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, on severely ill health he petitioned to resign his post; permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he petitioned to resign on account of grave illness, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 十年，病少瘳，命領刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, his illness slightly improved, and he was ordered to head the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, somewhat recovered, he was appointed Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 十一年春，復命署直隸總督，力辭，上勉之行。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eleventh year, he was again ordered to serve as acting governor-general of Zhili; he strenuously declined, and the emperor urged him to proceed.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eleventh year he was again ordered to serve as acting governor-general of Zhili; though he pleaded illness, the emperor pressed him to accept.

sentences.zh: 三月，卒於官，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: In the third month he died in office; funeral sacrifices and burial honors were granted.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office that third month and was granted state funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 執玉重民事，每請從寬大，疏入輒報可。

translations.literal: Zhiyu valued the people's affairs; he always petitioned for leniency, and his memorials upon submission were invariably approved.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyu cared deeply for the welfare of the people; his pleas for leniency were almost always granted.

sentences.zh: 執玉嘗曰：「吾才拙，政事不如人，可自力者勤耳。

translations.literal: Zhiyu once said: "My talent is dull; in governance I am not the equal of others—what I can exert is diligence alone.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyu once remarked: "I am no gifted administrator; others surpass me in statecraft—diligence is all I can offer.

sentences.zh: 勤必自儉始。

translations.literal: Diligence must begin with frugality.
translations.idiomatic: And diligence, he held, must begin with thrift.

sentences.zh: 」養廉歲用十三四，餘歸之司庫。

translations.literal: " Of his integrity stipend he used thirteen or fourteen taels per year; the remainder he returned to the provincial treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He spent only thirteen or fourteen taels of his annual integrity stipend and returned the rest to the provincial treasury.

sentences.zh: 楊永斌，字壽廷，雲南昆明人。

translations.literal: Yang Yongbin, courtesy name Shouting, was a native of Kunming, Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yongbin, styled Shouting, hailed from Kunming in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十八年舉人。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examination in Kangxi 38.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his juren degree in Kangxi 38.

sentences.zh: 以知縣發廣西，補臨桂知縣，以廉能聞。

translations.literal: He was dispatched to Guangxi as a magistrate, appointed magistrate of Lingui, and became known for integrity and competence.
translations.idiomatic: Assigned to Guangxi as a county magistrate, he served at Lingui and won a reputation for probity and ability.

sentences.zh: 遭喪去，服除，授直隸阜平知縣，署平山，調大城，皆有惠政。

translations.literal: On mourning for a parent he left office; when the mourning period ended he was appointed magistrate of Fuping in Zhili, acted at Pingshan, was transferred to Dacheng—all with benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his parents he was posted to Fuping in Zhili, served acting posts at Pingshan and Dacheng, and earned praise for humane governance at each.

sentences.zh: 以捕治內監陳永忠未即獲，奪官。

translations.literal: Because the palace eunuch Chen Yongzhong was not immediately captured when pursued, his office was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his post when he failed to capture the eunuch Chen Yongzhong promptly enough.

sentences.zh: 大城民乞巡撫疏留，會世宗即位，知永斌賢，許复官。

translations.literal: The people of Dacheng petitioned the governor to memorialize retaining him; coinciding with the Yongzheng Emperor's accession, knowing Yongbin's worth, restoration of office was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Dacheng petitioned the governor to keep him in office; when the Yongzheng Emperor came to the throne, recognizing Yongbin's merit, he was restored to rank.

sentences.zh: 遷涿州知州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Zhuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to prefect of Zhuozhou.

sentences.zh: 雍正三年，特諭永斌才守俱優，授貴州威寧知府。

translations.literal: In Yongzheng 3, the emperor specially decreed that Yongbin's talent and integrity were both excellent and appointed him prefect of Weining in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 3 the emperor singled out Yongbin for both talent and integrity and appointed him prefect of Weining in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 威寧界滇、蜀，諸土司虐使其眾，時出掠境外。

translations.literal: Weining bordered Yunnan and Sichuan; native chiefs abused their peoples and frequently raided beyond the border.
translations.idiomatic: Weining lay on the borders of Yunnan and Sichuan, where native chiefs oppressed their subjects and often raided neighboring territory.

sentences.zh: 烏蒙祿萬鍾、鎮雄隴慶侯尤強悍。

translations.literal: Lu Wanchong of Wumeng and Long Qinghou of Zhenxiong were especially fierce and powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wanchong of Wumeng and Long Qinghou of Zhenxiong were particularly formidable.

sentences.zh: 永斌被檄定界，單騎入諭其渠，陰使人偽為商賈，分道圖地形。

translations.literal: Yongbin was ordered by dispatch to fix the boundaries; he rode alone to admonish their chieftains, while secretly sending men disguised as merchants to map the terrain by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to fix the frontier, Yongbin rode alone to parley with the chieftains while secretly dispatching agents disguised as merchants to survey the terrain.

sentences.zh: 鄂爾泰督雲、貴，永斌以圖上，且曰：「二酋不懲，終為邊患。

translations.literal: Ortai governed Yunnan and Guizhou; Yongbin submitted the maps and said: "If these two chiefs are not punished, they will be a border trouble in the end.
translations.idiomatic: When Ortai became governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou, Yongbin submitted his maps with a warning: "Unless these two chiefs are brought to heel, they will remain a perpetual threat on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 萬鍾幼，諸土司未附。

translations.literal: Wanchong is young; the other native chiefs have not yet submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Wanchong is still young, and the other chiefs have not yet rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 今四川總督劾萬鍾不職，請發兵壓境，召萬鍾出就質。

translations.literal: Now the Sichuan governor-general has impeached Wanchong for malfeasance and requested troops be sent to press the border and summon Wanchong to come out for questioning.
translations.idiomatic: The governor-general of Sichuan has already impeached Wanchong for misrule and proposes massing troops on the border and summoning him to account.

sentences.zh: 不出，以兵入。

translations.literal: If he does not come out, send troops in.
translations.idiomatic: If he refuses, march in with force.

sentences.zh: 烏蒙平，鎮雄勢孤，亦且降。

translations.literal: Once Wumeng is pacified, Zhenxiong isolated in strength will also submit.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wumeng falls, isolated Zhenxiong will likely capitulate as well.

sentences.zh: 」鄂爾泰從之，召萬鍾不至，令游擊哈元生與永斌督兵入。

translations.literal: " Ortai followed this; summoning Wanchong, he did not come; Ortai ordered Ranger Ha Yuansheng and Yongbin to lead troops in.
translations.idiomatic: Ortai agreed; when Wanchong ignored the summons, he ordered Ranger Ha Yuansheng and Yongbin to lead the invasion.

sentences.zh: 萬鍾走鎮遠，與慶侯同詣四川降。

translations.literal: Wanchong fled to Zhenyuan and, together with Qinghou, went to Sichuan to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Wanchong fled toward Zhenyuan and, with Qinghou, surrendered in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 凡三十三日而事定。

translations.literal: In all, thirty-three days and the affair was settled.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign was concluded in thirty-three days.

sentences.zh: 米貼土婦陸氏為亂，鄂爾泰遣兵討之，永斌語元生曰：「賊以冕山、巴補為後路，事急則渡金沙江而逸。

translations.literal: Lady Lu of the Mitie native office raised rebellion; Ortai sent troops to suppress her; Yongbin told Yuansheng: "The rebels use Mianshan and Babu as a rear route; when pressed they will cross the Jinsha River and escape.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Lu of Mitie rebelled, Ortai sent troops against her; Yongbin advised Yuansheng: "The rebels rely on Mianshan and Babu as an escape route and will flee across the Jinsha River when hard pressed.

sentences.zh: 以重兵扼其前，奇兵越江攻之，賊可殲也。

translations.literal: With heavy troops blocking their front, and surprise troops crossing the river to attack them, the rebels can be annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: Block them with a main force while sending a flanking column across the river to cut them off—they can be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 」元生用其策，克米貼。

translations.literal: " Yuansheng used his plan and captured Mitie.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansheng adopted the plan and took Mitie.

sentences.zh: 鄂爾泰疏薦永斌可大用，擢貴東道，旋調糧驛道，署按察使。

translations.literal: Ortai memorialized recommending Yongbin for great employment; he was promoted to Guizhou East Circuit intendant, soon transferred to grain and relay intendant, and served as acting provincial judge.
translations.idiomatic: Ortai recommended Yongbin for higher office; he was promoted to Guizhou East Circuit intendant, then grain-and-relay intendant, and appointed acting provincial judge.

sentences.zh: 朝議加稅軍田畝五錢，永斌議曰：「軍田糧以屯租為準，已數倍於民田。

translations.literal: The court debated adding five qian tax per mu on military colony fields; Yongbin argued: "Military colony grain tax, reckoned by garrison rent, is already several times that of civilian fields.
translations.idiomatic: When the court proposed adding five qian per mu on military colony land, Yongbin objected: "Military fields are already taxed at several times the civilian rate under the garrison-rent system.

sentences.zh: 且今轉相授受，與民田交易無異。

translations.literal: Moreover, today they pass from hand to hand in succession, no different from transactions in civilian fields.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, these plots now change hands like ordinary farmland.

sentences.zh: 名為軍屯，實皆民產，而畝稅之，是重科也，民必不服。

translations.literal: Called military colonies in name, in fact all are the people's property—yet to tax by the mu is double exaction; the people will surely not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Though called military colonies, they are effectively private property; an additional per-mu levy would be oppressive and invite resistance.

sentences.zh: 當多事之秋，增剝膚之患，驅之為亂耳。

translations.literal: In a time of many troubles, to increase afflictions that flay the skin is only to drive them to rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In troubled times, piling new burdens on the people would only drive them to revolt.

sentences.zh: 」鄂爾泰以聞，事乃寢。

translations.literal: " Ortai reported this; the matter then lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Ortai relayed the objection, and the proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷湖南布政使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to Hunan provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he became treasurer of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 湖南方議清察軍田計畝，未定，永斌援貴州議以請，亦得免。

translations.literal: Hunan was then debating clearing and inspecting military colony fields for per-mu taxation, not yet decided; Yongbin cited the Guizhou deliberation in petition and exemption was granted as well.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan was considering the same per-mu levy on military land; Yongbin invoked his Guizhou precedent and secured exemption there too.

sentences.zh: 九年，調廣東。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was transferred to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 十年春，命署巡撫，是秋真除。

translations.literal: In the spring of the tenth year he was ordered to serve as acting governor; that autumn he received formal appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the tenth year he was made acting governor; he received formal appointment that autumn.

sentences.zh: 廣東生齒繁，民不勤稼穡，米值高。

translations.literal: Guangdong's population was dense; the people did not diligently cultivate grain; rice prices were high.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong was densely populated yet its people farmed little, keeping rice prices high.

sentences.zh: 永斌飭諸州縣勸墾，高亢不宜禾，令藝豆麥，諸山坡麓栽所宜木。

translations.literal: Yongbin ordered the prefectures and counties to encourage reclamation; where high and dry ground was unsuitable for rice, he ordered beans and wheat planted; on hillsides and foothills he had suitable trees planted.
translations.idiomatic: Yongbin ordered local officials to promote reclamation, planting beans and wheat on uplands unsuited to rice and orchards on hillsides and slopes.

sentences.zh: 又以惠、潮兩府民最悍，招墾官田，租入充粵秀書院膏火。
