translations.literal: He also noted that Huizhou and Chaozhou had the fiercest people; he invited reclamation of official lands, rent income to fund the Yuexiu Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In Huizhou and Chaozhou, where the populace was especially unruly, he opened official land for settlement, dedicating rent to the Yuexiu Academy.

sentences.zh: 奏聞，嘉獎，命勘明墾地畝數。

translations.literal: Upon memorializing, commendation was granted, and he was ordered to survey and clarify the mu count of reclaimed land.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the initiative and ordered a survey of reclaimed acreage.

sentences.zh: 尋又奏言：「勘明可墾地六千八百餘頃，此外或山深箐密，或夾沙帶鹵，體察民情，恐磽地薄收，糧賦無出。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized again: "Survey has clarified more than 6,800 qing of reclaimable land; beyond this, some areas are deep mountains with dense ravines, some sandy and salty—observing popular sentiment, I fear barren land with thin harvests cannot yield grain tax.
translations.idiomatic: He soon reported: "Some 6,800 qing can be reclaimed outright, but much else is steep, remote, sandy, or saline; peasants fear poor yields will leave them unable to pay tax.

sentences.zh: 臣思瘠田產穀雖少，若多墾數十萬畝，年豐可得數十萬石，即歉歲亦必稍有所獲，事益於民。

translations.literal: Your subject considers that though poor fields produce little grain, if several hundred thousand mu more are reclaimed, in abundant years several hundred thousand shi can be obtained, and even in lean years something will surely be gained—the matter benefits the people.
translations.idiomatic: Yet even marginal land adds up: reclaiming hundreds of thousands of mu could yield hundreds of thousands of shi in good years and something even in bad—a clear benefit to the people.

sentences.zh: 察通省糧額，新寧斥鹵，輕則畝徵銀四釐有奇、米四合有奇。

translations.literal: Examining the provincial grain quota, Xining's saline wasteland is taxed lightly, at a little more than four li of silver and a little more than four he of rice per mu.
translations.idiomatic: In Xining, saline wasteland is lightly taxed at slightly over four li of silver and four he of grain per mu.

sentences.zh: 擬請凡承墾磽瘠之地，概準此例，十年起科。

translations.literal: I propose requesting that for all who undertake reclamation of barren and poor land, this precedent apply uniformly, with taxation beginning after ten years.
translations.idiomatic: I propose applying that rate to all reclaimed poor land, with taxes due only after ten years.

sentences.zh: 」下部議行，於是墾田至百十八萬餘畝。

translations.literal: " It was referred to the ministry for deliberation and implementation; thus reclaimed fields reached more than 1.18 million mu.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry approved, and eventually more than 1.18 million mu were brought under cultivation.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，兼署兩廣總督。

translations.literal: In Qianlong 1, he concurrently served as acting governor-general of Liangguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianlong he served concurrently as acting governor-general of the Two Guang.

sentences.zh: 上命除落地稅，因請並免漁課、埠稅，革粵海關贏餘陋例未盡汰者，上悉從之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered abolition of the landing tax; he therefore requested simultaneous exemption of fishing levies and wharf taxes, and reform of corrupt surplus practices at the Guangdong Customs not yet fully eliminated—the emperor granted all.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor abolished the landing tax, Yongbin also asked to lift fishing and wharf duties and purge remaining corrupt surcharges at the Guangdong customs—and the emperor agreed to all of it.

sentences.zh: 永斌在廣東數年，坦懷虛己，淬厲諸將吏。

translations.literal: Yongbin in Guangdong for several years, open-hearted and humble, tempered and sharpened all commanders and officials.
translations.idiomatic: During his years in Guangdong, Yongbin governed with openness and humility while hardening his officers and staff.

sentences.zh: 獲劇盜餘猊、陳美倫數十輩置之法，收曲江乳源諸峒瑤歸化。

translations.literal: He captured dozens of major brigands such as Yu Ni and Chen Meilun and put them to law; he received the surrender and submission of Yao tribes in the dong settlements of Qujiang, Ruyuan, and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: He broke up bands led by the outlaw Yu Ni and Chen Meilun, putting dozens to justice, and brought Yao communities in Qujiang and Ruyuan back under the fold.

sentences.zh: 西洋估舶互市至者，悉令寄椗澳門，不得泊會城下。

translations.literal: Western merchant ships coming to trade were all ordered to anchor at Macau and not moor below the provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: Western trading vessels were required to anchor at Macau rather than the capital's harbor.

sentences.zh: 粵民頌其績。

translations.literal: The people of Guangdong praised his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Guangdong sang his praises.

sentences.zh: 二年，調湖北，兼署湖廣總督。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to Hubei, concurrently serving as acting governor-general of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was transferred to Hubei, also serving as acting governor-general of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 令嚴保甲，繕城堡，課農桑，實社倉，興學校，諸政畢舉。

translations.literal: He ordered strict household registration, repair of fortresses and walls, instruction in sericulture, filling of community granaries, establishment of schools—all policies fully carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He tightened household registration, repaired fortifications, promoted sericulture, stocked community granaries, and revived schools—implementing reforms across the board.

sentences.zh: 未幾，調江蘇。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 按行奉賢、南匯、上海、寶山四縣海塘，以築塘取土成渠，塘根浸損，議於塘內開河，南接華亭運河，北達寶山高橋。

translations.literal: Inspecting the sea dikes of Fengxian, Nanhui, Shanghai, and Baoshan counties, finding that digging earth for dike construction had formed channels that eroded the dike foundations, he proposed opening a canal inside the dike, south connecting to the Huating transport canal, north reaching Gaoshan in Baoshan.
translations.idiomatic: Inspecting sea walls in Fengxian, Nanhui, Shanghai, and Baoshan, he found that quarrying soil for repairs had undercut the embankments; he proposed digging an interior canal linking the Huating canal in the south to Gaoshan in Baoshan in the north.

sentences.zh: 又察華亭金山嘴、倪家路，寶山楊家嘴地當衝要，議視地所宜，或增築石壩，或就舊塘加築寬厚，或改築石塘。

translations.literal: He also inspected Jinshan Mouth and Niijia Road in Huating, and Yangjia Mouth in Baoshan, where the terrain was critical, and proposed according to local suitability either adding stone dams, thickening old dikes, or rebuilding stone seawalls.
translations.idiomatic: At critical points such as Jinshan Mouth and Niijia Road in Huating and Yangjia Mouth in Baoshan, he recommended stone groins, thickened embankments, or new stone seawalls as terrain required.

sentences.zh: 又請於寶山建海神廟。

translations.literal: He also requested building a Sea God temple at Baoshan.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed a Sea God temple at Baoshan.

sentences.zh: 並從之。

translations.literal: All were granted.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 三年，以老病乞休，召詣京師，署禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year, on account of age and illness he petitioned to retire; he was summoned to the capital and served as acting vice minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he retired on grounds of age and illness, was recalled to the capital, and appointed acting vice minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 尋授吏部。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made vice minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 四年，致仕。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he retired from service.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he retired from office.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he died.

sentences.zh: 孫，廕生，初授主事，官至江蘇按察使。

translations.literal: His grandson, by inherited privilege, was first appointed a department director and rose to provincial judge of Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson entered service by privilege as a department director and rose to Jiangsu provincial judge.

sentences.zh: 論曰：其倬、宗仁、毓珣，皆聖祖所擢用，丕著勳勚；

translations.literal: The commentator says: Qizhuo, Zongren, and Yuxun were all promoted by the Shenzu Emperor and greatly distinguished themselves in service;
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: Qizhuo, Zongren, and Yuxun were all raised up by the Kangxi Emperor and won great distinction in office;

sentences.zh: 世宗畀以兼圻，忠誠靡懈，恩禮​​始終，宜矣！

translations.literal: the Shizong Emperor entrusted them with broad jurisdictions; their loyalty never slackened and imperial favor endured to the end—as was fitting!
translations.idiomatic: the Yongzheng Emperor entrusted them with broad jurisdictions; their loyalty never slackened and imperial favor endured to the end—as was only fitting!

sentences.zh: 幰度居官不擾民，執玉、永斌尤懃懃施惠，文乾、宗錫能濟其美。

translations.literal: Xiandu in office did not harass the people; Zhiyu and Yongbin were especially diligent in bestowing benefits, and Wenqian and Zongxi were able to complement their excellence.
translations.idiomatic: Xiandu governed without harassing the people; Zhiyu and Yongbin were especially diligent in bringing benefits, and Wenqian and Zongxi helped complete their good work.

sentences.zh: 世宗治尚明肅，諸臣皆以開敏精勤稱上指，為政持大體，與夫急功近名，流於谿刻，重為世詬病者，固大異矣。

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor's governance prized clarity and severity; these officials were all quick, perceptive, and diligent in meeting his intent, holding to the larger principles in government—quite unlike those who sought quick fame, slid into harsh pettiness, and were heavily censured by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzheng's reign prized clarity and severity; these officials were quick, perceptive, and diligent in meeting his intent and held to the larger principles of government—quite unlike those who chased quick fame, slid into harsh pettiness, and drew heavy censure from their own age.
